title: Case study: sudden infant deaths in North Carolina
text: file nc.shp sf holds one polygon per county , two periods (1974-78 1979-84), number live births (BIR74, BIR79), number SIDS deaths (SID74, SID79) number non-white live births (NWBIR74, NWBIR79). sf documents North Carolina SIDS sample data (?sf::nc); counts analysed spatial clustering Cressie Read (1985) Cressie Chan (1989). polygons stored longitude latitude (NAD27). Transform North Carolina state plane (EPSG 32119), planar system metres, boundaries centroids computed flat map. analysis uses first period. deaths rare: county births may record none, raw rate county says little. Risk compared expected count EiE_i: number deaths county ii every county shared statewide rate, Ei=Bi∑jDj/∑jBjE_i = B_i \sum_j D_j / \sum_j B_j, BiB_i births DiD_i deaths county ii. ratio Di/EiD_i / E_i standardised mortality ratio (SMR). covariate share non-white births, centred mean across counties multiplied 10, coefficient change log relative risk per 10 percentage points.   mean non-white share across counties 31.2%. SMR runs zero, 13 counties without recorded death, 4.73, neighbouring counties often fall classes far apart. High SMRs gather north-east south state, two regions non-white share highest.

code: rr_draws <- function(fit, E, n = 4000) {   w   <- tulpa_outer_grid(fit)$weights   k   <- sample(seq_along(w), n, replace = TRUE, prob = w)   m   <- fit$fitted_eta[k, , drop = FALSE]   s   <- sqrt(fit$fitted_eta_var[k, , drop = FALSE])   eta <- m + s * matrix(rnorm(length(m)), nrow(m))   sweep(exp(eta), 2, E, "/") } set.seed(1) th <- rr_draws(fit_bym2, d$E) nc$rr      <- colMeans(th) nc$rr_sd   <- apply(th, 2, sd) nc$p_exc   <- colMeans(th > 1) summary(nc$rr) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.5236  0.6916  1.0085  1.0686  1.2930  2.5092 round(range(nc$rr[nc$SID74 == 0]), 2) #> [1] 0.52 1.49 plot(nc["rr"], breaks = br, pal = hcl.colors(6, "Blue-Red 3"),      main = "Relative risk, BYM2 posterior mean", key.pos = 1) plot(nc["rr_sd"], pal = function(k) hcl.colors(k, "Purples 3", rev = TRUE),      main = "Posterior SD of the relative risk", key.pos = 1) summary(nc$rr_sd) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>  0.1223  0.1600  0.2185  0.2471  0.3011  0.6609 nc$NAME[which.max(nc$rr_sd)] #> [1] "Anson" round(cor(nc$rr, nc$rr_sd), 2) #> [1] 0.89 plot(nc["p_exc"], breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.8, 0.95, 1),      pal = hcl.colors(5, "Blue-Red 3"),      main = "P(relative risk > 1)", key.pos = 1) sum(nc$p_exc > 0.95) #> [1] 17 sum(nc$p_exc < 0.05) #> [1] 26 head(st_drop_geometry(nc)[order(-nc$p_exc),                           c("NAME", "SID74", "smr", "rr", "p_exc")], 5) #>           NAME SID74      smr       rr   p_exc #> 5  Northampton     9 3.133189 2.504229 1.00000 #> 16     Halifax    18 2.467994 2.077676 1.00000 #> 85       Anson    15 4.726392 2.509231 1.00000 #> 94     Robeson    31 1.943918 2.108026 1.00000 #> 28      Bertie     6 2.241823 2.112305 0.99975

code: set.seed(1) n_h   <- 600 elev  <- rnorm(n_h) water <- rnorm(n_h) eta_f <- 0.4 + 1.2 * elev + 0.8 * water   # forest vs wetland eta_g <- 0.6 + 0.3 * elev + 1.0 * water   # grassland vs wetland P_h   <- cbind(exp(eta_f), exp(eta_g), 1) P_h   <- P_h / rowSums(P_h) hab_lev <- c("forest", "grassland", "wetland") habitat <- apply(P_h, 1, function(p) sample(hab_lev, 1, prob = p)) dh <- data.frame(habitat = factor(habitat, levels = hab_lev),                  elev = elev, water = water) table(dh$habitat) #>  #>    forest grassland   wetland  #>       208       226       166

Averaged five data sets, censored truncated fits return slopes 0.6 0.58 true 0.6. substituted fit averages 0.54 Gaussian fit truncated data 0.45. figure shows five estimates fit.
code: one_rep <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   r <- data.frame(site = d$site, x = rnorm(N))   u_r <- rnorm(G, 0, 0.4)   r$y_star <- 1 + 0.6 * r$x + u_r[as.integer(r$site)] + rnorm(N, 0, 0.5)   b <- r$y_star < lod   r$y     <- ifelse(b, lod, r$y_star)   r$lower <- ifelse(b, NA, r$y_star)   r$upper <- ifelse(b, lod, r$y_star)   r$y_sub <- ifelse(b, lod - log(2), r$y_star)   k <- r[r$y_star <= 1.5, ]   fit <- function(f, data) {     tulpa(f, data = data, family = "gaussian", control = ctl)   }   fits <- list(     censored      = fit(y | cens(lower, upper) ~ x + (1 | site), r),     substituted   = fit(y_sub ~ x + (1 | site), r),     truncated     = fit(y_star | trunc(ub = 1.5) ~ x + (1 | site), k),     kept_gaussian = fit(y_star ~ x + (1 | site), k))   t(sapply(fits, function(f) row_of(f)[c("slope", "resid_sd")])) } reps <- lapply(11:15, one_rep) slope <- sapply(reps, function(r) r[, "slope"]) sd_hat <- sapply(reps, function(r) r[, "resid_sd"]) round(slope, 3) #>                [,1]  [,2]  [,3]  [,4]  [,5] #> censored      0.592 0.649 0.578 0.598 0.605 #> substituted   0.548 0.539 0.540 0.541 0.524 #> truncated     0.617 0.562 0.534 0.627 0.570 #> kept_gaussian 0.458 0.472 0.403 0.478 0.436 round(cbind(mean_slope = rowMeans(slope), mean_resid_sd = rowMeans(sd_hat)), 3) #>               mean_slope mean_resid_sd #> censored           0.604         0.506 #> substituted        0.538         0.545 #> truncated          0.582         0.495 #> kept_gaussian      0.449         0.430 op <- par(mar = c(4, 8, 1, 1)) plot(slope, rep(1:4, 5), pch = rep(c(19, 1, 17, 2), 5),      yaxt = "n", ylim = c(0.5, 4.5), xlab = "slope estimate", ylab = "") axis(2, at = 1:4, labels = rownames(slope), las = 1) abline(v = 0.6, lty = 2) par(op)

text: control$checkpoint = list(path =, resume =) takes file whether continue . path given, resume defaults TRUE; resume = FALSE removes existing file starts . example binomial model intrinsic CAR field chain 30 regions, fitted nested Laplace mode = "structured". fit_ckpt() wraps call later sections can repeat data another resume. file starts header holding fingerprint inputs: response, trial counts, design matrix, offsets, field’s structure solver settings. solved grid cell follows one record, keyed hyperparameter coordinate closed checksum key payload.
code: set.seed(20260716) S <- 30L W <- matrix(0, S, S) for (i in 1:(S - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 df <- data.frame(region = factor(seq_len(S))) df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 10 + rnorm(S, 0, 0.3) df$y <- rbinom(S, 20, plogis(-0.4 + 0.5 * df$x))  ckpt <- tempfile(fileext = ".ckpt") fit_ckpt <- function(data, resume) {   tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = data, family = "binomial",         n_trials = rep(20L, S), spatial = spatial_car(W, level = "obs"),         mode = "structured",         control = list(n_threads = 2,                        checkpoint = list(path = ckpt, resume = resume))) } fit <- fit_ckpt(df, resume = FALSE) #> [nested-laplace] 1/9 cells (11%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 6/6 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 1/5 cells (20%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells coef(fit) #> (Intercept)           x  #>  -0.2760639   0.4225753 full_size <- file.size(ckpt) full_size #> [1] 80536

what: Random-intercept GLMM: tulpa, lme4 and glmmTMB
title: Compatibility with lme4, glmmTMB, brms and INLA
text: binary response measured 40 groups 8 setting Laplace approximation group’s integral least accurate, demanding first test. intercept -0.4, slope 0.9, group intercepts drawn SD 0.8. lme4 glmmTMB maximise Laplace-approximated likelihood fixed effects random-intercept SD. tulpa backend mode = "agq": n_quad = 1 marginal joint Laplace approximation, tol tightens optimiser (default tolerance discussed Differences). tulpa glmmTMB reach log-likelihood four decimals, glmer’s default optimiser stops 0.0007 . table therefore compares estimates glmmTMB. random-intercept SD standard error either package’s default output, last two columns empty. match holds adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature. lme4 calls number nodes nAGQ; tulpa calls n_quad. seven nodes integral group eight binary responses longer Laplace approximation, SD estimate moves 0.816 0.842 packages.
code: G <- 40L; npg <- 8L g <- rep(seq_len(G), each = npg) x <- rnorm(G * npg) u <- rnorm(G, sd = 0.8) y <- rbinom(G * npg, 1, plogis(-0.4 + 0.9 * x + u[g])) d <- data.frame(y = y, x = x, g = factor(g)) tm <- list() tm$tulpa_agq <- system.time(   f_t <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "binomial", mode = "agq",                control = list(n_quad = 1L, tol = 1e-10)) )[["elapsed"]] summary(f_t)$coefficients[, 1:2] #>               estimate std.error #> (Intercept) -0.4873948 0.1864441 #> x            0.9396841 0.1568559 f_t$sigma_re #> [1] 0.8160032 tm$glmer <- system.time(   f_l <- lme4::glmer(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = binomial) )[["elapsed"]] tm$glmmTMB <- system.time(   f_g <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = binomial) )[["elapsed"]] c(logLik_tulpa = f_t$log_marginal, logLik_glmer = as.numeric(logLik(f_l)),   logLik_glmmTMB = as.numeric(logLik(f_g))) #>   logLik_tulpa   logLik_glmer logLik_glmmTMB  #>      -186.8587      -186.8594      -186.8587 se_g <- sqrt(diag(vcov(f_g)$cond)) tab_ml <- agree(   c(coef(f_t), sigma = f_t$sigma_re),   c(summary(f_t)$coefficients[, "std.error"], NA),   c(glmmTMB::fixef(f_g)$cond, sigma = sqrt(glmmTMB::VarCorr(f_g)$cond$g[1])),   c(se_g, NA)) round(tab_ml, 5) #>                tulpa tulpa_se    other other_se diff diff_in_se #> (Intercept) -0.48739  0.18644 -0.48740  0.18645    0      0e+00 #> x            0.93968  0.15686  0.93968  0.15686    0     -1e-05 #> sigma        0.81600       NA  0.81600       NA    0         NA f_t7 <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "binomial", mode = "agq",               control = list(n_quad = 7L, tol = 1e-10)) f_l7 <- lme4::glmer(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = binomial, nAGQ = 7) rbind(tulpa = c(coef(f_t7), sigma = f_t7$sigma_re),       glmer = c(lme4::fixef(f_l7), sigma = attr(lme4::VarCorr(f_l7)$g, "stddev"))) #>       (Intercept)         x     sigma #> tulpa  -0.4891310 0.9406283 0.8418408 #> glmer  -0.4891226 0.9406310 0.8418574

title: Compatibility with lme4, glmmTMB, brms and INLA
text: random slope adds covariance matrix: intercept SD, slope SD correlation. lme4 fits Poisson response well, glmmTMB also offers restricted likelihood, estimand tulpa’s empirical-Bayes backend. Simulate 60 groups 12 counts SDs 0.7 0.5 correlation 0.4. mode = "eb" maximises Laplace marginal covariance fixed effects integrated , restricted (REML-type) estimate. hyperprior = "flat" removes default PC LKJ prior covariance, nothing likelihood enters maximisation; fixed effects keep default normal(0, 2.5) prior, weak 720 observations. glmmTMB call formula REML = TRUE. SDs correlation agree 1e-4, fixed effects differ hundredth standard error. Bayesian counterpart integrates covariance instead fixing maximum. mode = "laplace" slope term routes integration (Random slopes article covers ). posterior medians two SDs equal restricted estimates two decimals, median correlation 0.52 restricted 0.57, inside interval 0.25 0.73.
code: G2 <- 60L; npg2 <- 12L g2 <- rep(seq_len(G2), each = npg2) x2 <- rnorm(G2 * npg2) Sig <- matrix(c(0.49, 0.14, 0.14, 0.25), 2) b2 <- t(t(chol(Sig)) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * G2), 2)) y2 <- rpois(G2 * npg2, exp(0.2 + 0.5 * x2 + b2[g2, 1] + b2[g2, 2] * x2)) d2 <- data.frame(y = y2, x = x2, g = factor(g2)) tm$tulpa_eb <- system.time(   s_t <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | g), data = d2, family = "poisson",                mode = "eb", hyperprior = "flat") )[["elapsed"]] tm$glmmTMB_reml <- system.time(   s_g <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(y ~ x + (1 + x | g), data = d2, family = poisson,                           REML = TRUE) )[["elapsed"]] vc <- glmmTMB::VarCorr(s_g)$cond$g tab_rs <- agree(   c(coef(s_t), sd_int = s_t$map$sigma[1], sd_x = s_t$map$sigma[2],     cor = s_t$map$rho),   c(summary(s_t)$coefficients[, "std.error"], NA, NA, NA),   c(glmmTMB::fixef(s_g)$cond, attr(vc, "stddev"),     cor = attr(vc, "correlation")[1, 2]),   c(sqrt(diag(vcov(s_g)$cond)), NA, NA, NA)) round(tab_rs, 5) #>               tulpa tulpa_se   other other_se     diff diff_in_se #> (Intercept) 0.36146  0.09205 0.36216  0.09268 -0.00070   -0.00752 #> x           0.37336  0.08274 0.37397  0.08370 -0.00061   -0.00734 #> sd_int      0.66035       NA 0.66030       NA  0.00005         NA #> sd_x        0.57221       NA 0.57218       NA  0.00003         NA #> cor         0.56860       NA 0.56850       NA  0.00010         NA s_n <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | g), data = d2, family = "poisson",              mode = "laplace", control = list(n_threads = 2)) summary(s_n)$hyperparameters[1:3, c("parameter", "median", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")] #>   parameter    median     ci_lo     ci_hi #> 1   sigma_1 0.6618372 0.5385379 0.8241984 #> 2   sigma_2 0.5730461 0.4599580 0.7214724 #> 3    rho_12 0.5227020 0.2459051 0.7251218

what: Areal BYM2 model: tulpa and INLA
title: Compatibility with lme4, glmmTMB, brms and INLA
text: BYM2 model splits region’s effect scaled ICAR part independent part, total SD sigma mixing weight structured share. INLA calls weight phi parameterises scale precision; tulpa calls weight rho reports sigma directly. scale ICAR part marginal variances geometric mean one (Riebler et al. 2016), spatial_bym2() INLA’s scale.model = TRUE . Simulate Poisson counts 10 10 lattice regions rook adjacency, expected counts 10 60, slope 0.4 field total SD 0.6, 70% variance spatially structured.
code: nr <- 10L; K <- nr * nr W <- matrix(0, K, K) id <- function(i, j) (i - 1L) * nr + j for (i in 1:nr) for (j in 1:nr) {   if (i < nr) W[id(i, j), id(i + 1L, j)] <- W[id(i + 1L, j), id(i, j)] <- 1   if (j < nr) W[id(i, j), id(i, j + 1L)] <- W[id(i, j + 1L), id(i, j)] <- 1 } cx <- rep(1:nr, each = nr); cy <- rep(1:nr, nr) s  <- as.numeric(scale(sin(cx / 3) + cos(cy / 3))) bf <- 0.6 * (sqrt(0.7) * s + sqrt(0.3) * rnorm(K)) x3 <- rnorm(K); E <- round(runif(K, 10, 60)) y3 <- rpois(K, E * exp(-0.3 + 0.4 * x3 + bf)) d3 <- data.frame(y = y3, x = x3, E = E, region = factor(1:K), id = 1:K)

code: Tt    <- 20 time  <- sample(seq_len(Tt), n, replace = TRUE) trend <- sin(2 * pi * seq_len(Tt) / Tt) dt <- data.frame(y = rpois(n, exp(0.3 + 0.5 * x + trend[time])),                  x = x, time = time) fit_t <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = dt, family = "poisson",                temporal = temporal_rw1("time"),                control = list(n_threads = 2)) #> [nested-laplace] 1/9 cells (11%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.02s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 6/6 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells fit_t #> tulpa nested-Laplace fit  #>   hyperparameters: tau  (grid: 12 cells) #>   outer pareto-k: -1.44 (reliable) #>   fit in 0.4s (grid 0.0s) #> Device: inference=cpu, laplace_dense=cpu, sparse_cholesky=cpu #> Call: tulpa(formula = y ~ x, data = dt, family = "poisson", temporal = temporal_rw1("time"), control = list(n_threads = 2)) #>   n_obs: 300  #>  #> Coefficients: #> (Intercept)           x  #>      0.2637      0.5215  #>  #> Use summary() for intervals, variance components, hyperparameters and reliability. og <- tulpa_outer_grid(fit_t) data.frame(tau = round(og$nodes[, 1], 2), weight = round(og$weights, 3)) #>      tau weight #> 1   0.30  0.000 #> 2   0.53  0.000 #> 3   0.95  0.000 #> 4   1.69  0.004 #> 5   3.00  0.050 #> 6   5.33  0.184 #> 7   9.49  0.226 #> 8  16.87  0.064 #> 9  30.00  0.002 #> 10  7.11  0.252 #> 11 12.65  0.127 #> 12  4.00  0.092 library(ggplot2) ggplot(data.frame(tau = og$nodes[, 1], weight = og$weights),        aes(tau, weight)) +   geom_segment(aes(xend = tau, yend = 0), colour = "steelblue") +   geom_point() +   scale_x_log10() +   labs(x = "tau (log scale)", y = "cell weight") +   theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),         plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "transparent"))

Build grid adjacency first: two regions neighbours share edge. true field smooth surface grid, scaled standard deviation 0.6 log scale. intercept 0.5 slope 0.4. Six hundred observations spread random regions, carries survey year 1 10 effect counts; year temporal check. d holds responses (y Poisson, y_od overdispersed), covariate, region factor, year grid coordinates cx, cy observation’s region. code: side  <- 6L K     <- side^2 cells <- expand.grid(col = 1:side, row = 1:side) dmat  <- abs(outer(cells$col, cells$col, "-")) +          abs(outer(cells$row, cells$row, "-")) W     <- (dmat == 1) * 1 set.seed(1) field_true <- 0.6 * as.numeric(scale(sin(cells$col / 2) +                                      cos(cells$row / 2))) n      <- 600 region <- sample(1:K, n, replace = TRUE) x      <- rnorm(n) year   <- sample(1:10, n, replace = TRUE) mu     <- exp(0.5 + 0.4 * x + field_true[region]) y      <- rpois(n, mu) y_od   <- rnbinom(n, mu = mu, size = 1.5) d <- data.frame(y = y, y_od = y_od, x = x, region = factor(region),                 year = year, cx = cells$col[region], cy = cells$row[region]) sp  <- list(type = "icar", adjacency = W) ctl <- list(n_threads = 2) fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = d, family = "poisson",              spatial = sp, mode = "nested_laplace", control = ctl) #> [nested-laplace] 1/9 cells (11%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells fit_od <- tulpa(y_od ~ x + spatial(region), data = d, family = "poisson",                 spatial = sp, mode = "nested_laplace", control = ctl) #> [nested-laplace] 1/9 cells (11%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells rbind(correct = coef(fit), misspecified = coef(fit_od)) #>              (Intercept)         x #> correct        0.5294855 0.4036127 #> misspecified   0.5989578 0.4345329

code: n          <- 300 gamma_true <- c(0.8, -1.0)   # logit P(at risk): intercept, slope on v beta_true  <- c(1.0, 0.5)    # log expected count: intercept, slope on x  sim_zip <- function(n) {   x <- rnorm(n)   v <- rnorm(n)   z <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(gamma_true[1] + gamma_true[2] * v))   y <- z * rpois(n, exp(beta_true[1] + beta_true[2] * x))   list(y = y, X = cbind(1, x), Z = cbind(1, v), z = z) }  set.seed(20261102) dat <- sim_zip(n) c(structural_zeros = mean(dat$z == 0), observed_zeros = mean(dat$y == 0)) #> structural_zeros   observed_zeros  #>        0.3300000        0.4266667

title: EM + Laplace
text: e_step(fits, ...) receives current block fits, named list tulpa_laplace() results whose $mode holds coefficients, returns list(weights = ...). first iteration fits empty list, callback returns starting guess: every zero 0.5. m_step_encode(weights, ...) returns one block per GLM, list y, X, family weights. factory builds one dataset, code serves replication . binomial block carries soft labels weights, never fractional y; ?tulpa_em_laplace explains fractional response different objective refused.
code: zip_callbacks <- function(d) {   y <- d$y; X <- d$X; Z <- d$Z; n <- length(y)   e_step <- function(fits, ...) {     if (!length(fits)) return(list(weights = ifelse(y > 0, 1, 0.5)))     eta <- drop(Z %*% fits$occ$mode)     log_p0 <- plogis(eta, log.p = TRUE) - exp(drop(X %*% fits$abund$mode))     list(weights = ifelse(y > 0, 1,                          plogis(log_p0 - plogis(-eta, log.p = TRUE))))   }   m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) list(     occ   = list(y = rep(c(1, 0), each = n), X = rbind(Z, Z),                  weights = c(weights, 1 - weights), family = "binomial"),     abund = list(y = y, X = X, weights = weights, family = "poisson")   )   list(e_step = e_step, m_step_encode = m_step_encode) } cb <- zip_callbacks(dat)

title: EM + Laplace
text: tulpa_em_laplace() alternates two callbacks largest relative change coefficient falls tol (default 1e-4). E-step weights damped iterations, (1 - d) * new + d * previous damping = 0.3 default. fit$history records change per iteration:  change falls nearly constant factor per iteration, linear convergence EM. block fit carries mode H_beta, curvature weighted M-step objective mode. inverse gives standard error treats final weights known. abundance coefficients sit within 1.3 standard errors truth. zero-inflation slope γ1\gamma_1 estimated -0.67 truth -1.0, two standard errors away; one dataset can chance, replication measures often.
code: fit <- tulpa_em_laplace(cb$e_step, cb$m_step_encode, verbose = FALSE) c(converged = fit$converged, iterations = fit$n_iter) #>  converged iterations  #>          1         19 plot(fit$history$iter[-1], fit$history$delta[-1], log = "y", type = "b",      pch = 19, xlab = "EM iteration", ylab = "max relative change") abline(h = 1e-4, lty = 2) em_table <- function(fit) {   est <- c(fit$fits$occ$mode, fit$fits$abund$mode)   se  <- c(sqrt(diag(solve(fit$fits$occ$H_beta))),            sqrt(diag(solve(fit$fits$abund$H_beta))))   data.frame(est = est, se = se) } coef_names <- c("gamma0", "gamma1", "beta0", "beta1") truth <- c(gamma_true, beta_true) plain <- em_table(fit) round(data.frame(truth, plain, row.names = coef_names), 3) #>        truth    est    se #> gamma0   0.8  0.610 0.127 #> gamma1  -1.0 -0.671 0.138 #> beta0    1.0  1.021 0.045 #> beta1    0.5  0.450 0.041

code: zip_mle <- function(d) {   nll <- function(p) {     psi <- plogis(drop(d$Z %*% p[1:2]))     lam <- exp(drop(d$X %*% p[3:4]))     -sum(ifelse(d$y == 0, log(1 - psi + psi * exp(-lam)),                 log(psi) + dpois(d$y, lam, log = TRUE)))   }   o <- optim(rep(0, 4), nll, method = "BFGS", hessian = TRUE)   data.frame(est = o$par, se = sqrt(diag(solve(o$hessian)))) } exact <- zip_mle(dat) round(data.frame(em_est = plain$est, mle_est = exact$est,             em_se = plain$se, mle_se = exact$se, row.names = coef_names), 3) #>        em_est mle_est em_se mle_se #> gamma0  0.610   0.613 0.127  0.150 #> gamma1 -0.671  -0.675 0.138  0.160 #> beta0   1.021   1.021 0.045  0.051 #> beta1   0.450   0.451 0.041  0.044

code: re_one <- function(J, seed, m = 10, sigma = 0.7) {   set.seed(seed)   grp <- rep(seq_len(J), each = m)   b <- rnorm(J, 0, sigma)   x <- rnorm(J * m)   d <- data.frame(y = rpois(J * m, exp(0.3 + 0.5 * x + b[grp])),                   x = x, g = factor(grp))   f <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | g), data = d, family = "poisson",              mode = "structured", control = list(n_threads = 2))   h <- summary(f)$hyperparameters   h <- h[h$parameter == "sigma_1", ]   data.frame(J = J, seed = seed, mean = h$mean, lo = h$ci_lo, hi = h$ci_hi) } J_set <- c(3, 5, 10, 20, 40) re <- do.call(rbind, lapply(J_set, function(J) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(1:20, function(s) re_one(J, s))) })) re$covers <- re$lo <= 0.7 & re$hi >= 0.7 re_tab <- aggregate(cbind(covers, width = hi - lo) ~ J, data = re,                     FUN = function(v) round(median(v), 2)) re_tab$covers <- aggregate(covers ~ J, data = re, FUN = sum)$covers re_tab #>    J covers width #> 1  3     20  1.61 #> 2  5     19  1.21 #> 3 10     20  0.85 #> 4 20     19  0.52 #> 5 40     20  0.39 xpos <- match(re$J, J_set) + (re$seed - 10.5) / 30 plot(xpos, re$mean, ylim = range(c(re$lo, re$hi)), pch = 19, cex = 0.5,      xaxt = "n", xlab = "number of groups J",      ylab = "random-effect SD") axis(1, at = seq_along(J_set), labels = J_set) segments(xpos, re$lo, xpos, re$hi, col = "grey40") abline(h = 0.7, lty = 2, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue")

code: lattice <- function(k) {   W <- matrix(0, k * k, k * k)   id <- function(i, j) (i - 1) * k + j   for (i in 1:k) for (j in 1:k) {     if (i < k) W[id(i, j), id(i + 1, j)] <- W[id(i + 1, j), id(i, j)] <- 1     if (j < k) W[id(i, j), id(i, j + 1)] <- W[id(i, j + 1), id(i, j)] <- 1   }   W } draw_bym2 <- function(W, sigma, rho) {   e <- eigen(diag(rowSums(W)) - W, symmetric = TRUE)   keep <- e$values > 1e-8   V <- e$vectors[, keep]   Qinv <- V %*% (t(V) / e$values[keep])   scale_u <- exp(mean(log(diag(Qinv))))   u <- as.numeric(V %*% (rnorm(sum(keep)) / sqrt(e$values[keep])))   sigma * (sqrt(rho) * u / sqrt(scale_u) + sqrt(1 - rho) * rnorm(nrow(W))) } bym2_one <- function(k, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   W <- lattice(k)   phi <- draw_bym2(W, sigma = 0.6, rho = 0.5)   r <- rep(seq_len(k * k), each = 10)   x <- rnorm(length(r))   d <- data.frame(y = rpois(length(r), exp(1 + 0.3 * x + phi[r])),                   x = x, region = factor(r))   f <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = d, family = "poisson",              spatial = spatial_bym2(W, group_var = "region"),              mode = "nested_laplace", control = list(n_threads = 2))   h <- summary(f)$hyperparameters   cbind(K = k * code: nr <- 10L; nc <- 10L; S <- nr * nc rc <- expand.grid(r = seq_len(nr), c = seq_len(nc)) nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s)   which(abs(rc$r - rc$r[s]) + abs(rc$c - rc$c[s]) == 1)) nn <- lengths(nb) graph <- list(n_spatial_units = S, adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)),               adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L, n_neighbors = nn) W <- matrix(0, S, S) for (s in seq_len(S)) W[s, nb[[s]]] <- 1 sim_fields <- function(rho, s1 = 1, s2 = 0.8) {   Sigma <- matrix(c(s1^2, rho * s1 * s2, rho * s1 * s2, s2^2), 2)   R <- chol(diag(nn) - 0.99 * W)   z <- sapply(1:2, function(k) backsolve(R, rnorm(S)))   f <- z %*% chol(Sigma)   sweep(f, 2, colMeans(f)) } sim_obs <- function(f) {   s1 <- rep(seq_len(S), each = 3L); x1 <- rnorm(length(s1))   visited <- sort(sample(S, 70L))   s2 <- rep(visited, each = 3L); x2 <- rnorm(length(s2))   list(f = f, visited = visited, s1 = s1, x1 = x1, s2 = s2, x2 = x2,        y1 = rpois(length(s1), exp(0.5 + 0.4 * x1 + f[s1, 1])),        y2 = rbinom(length(s2), 10L, plogis(-0.3 + 0.8 * x2 + f[s2, 2]))) } set.seed(1) dat <- sim_obs(sim_fields(rho = 0.6)) c(cor = cor(dat$f)[1, 2], sd1 = sd(dat$f[, 1]), sd2 = sd(dat$f[, 2])) #>       cor       sd1       sd2  #> 0.5472979 0.8024354 0.8760067

code: rho_interval <- function(seed, rho) {   set.seed(seed)   d <- sim_obs(sim_fields(rho))   b <- c(mcar_block(d), list(logchol_grid = logchol))   f <- tulpa_nested_laplace_joint(make_arms(d), list(b), control = ctl)   og <- tulpa_outer_grid(f)   p <- tapply(og$weights, round(sigma_rho(og$nodes)[, "rho"], 1), sum)   lev <- as.numeric(names(p)); cw <- cumsum(p)   c(rho = rho, seed = seed, lo = lev[which(cw >= 0.025)[1]],     median = lev[which(cw >= 0.5)[1]], hi = lev[which(cw >= 0.975)[1]]) } rep_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(0.6, 0), function(r)   t(sapply(11:14, rho_interval, rho = r)))) rep_tab #>      rho seed   lo median  hi #> [1,] 0.6   11 -0.1    0.4 0.7 #> [2,] 0.6   12  0.2    0.5 0.7 #> [3,] 0.6   13  0.2    0.6 0.8 #> [4,] 0.6   14  0.2    0.5 0.8 #> [5,] 0.0   11 -0.7   -0.3 0.1 #> [6,] 0.0   12 -0.4   -0.1 0.2 #> [7,] 0.0   13 -0.3    0.0 0.4 #> [8,] 0.0   14 -0.2    0.1 0.4 k <- seq_len(nrow(rep_tab)) plot(k, rep_tab[, "median"], pch = 19, ylim = c(-1, 1), xaxt = "n",      xlab = "", ylab = "rho: median and 95% interval") segments(k, rep_tab[, "lo"], k, rep_tab[, "hi"]) axis(1, at = k, labels = paste0("rho=", rep_tab[, "rho"], "\nseed ",                                 rep_tab[, "seed"]), padj = 0.5, cex.axis = 0.7) abline(h = c(0.6, 0), lty = 2, col = c("darkorange", "steelblue"))

code: set.seed(4) S <- 6; Tn <- 30 ar_path <- function() {   as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.8), Tn, sd = 0.4 * sqrt(1 - 0.8^2))) } d2 <- data.frame(site = factor(rep(1:S, each = Tn)), year = rep(1:Tn, S),                  x = rnorm(S * Tn)) d2$eta <- 1 + 0.3 * d2$x + unlist(replicate(S, ar_path(), simplify = FALSE)) d2$y   <- rpois(nrow(d2), exp(d2$eta)) held <- d2$year > 25 | d2$year %in% 12:13 d2_na <- d2 d2_na$y[held] <- NA fit_ts <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = d2_na, family = "poisson",                 temporal = temporal_ar1("year", group_var = "site"),                 mode = "auto", control = list(progress = FALSE)) summary(fit_ts)$hyperparameters[, c("parameter", "median", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")] #>   parameter    median     ci_lo      ci_hi #> 1       tau 8.7624673 4.1072177 23.5457521 #> 2       rho 0.7270145 0.4602468  0.9007093 lp_ts <- posterior_linpred(fit_ts, summary = TRUE) yrep_ts <- posterior_predict(fit_ts, ndraws = 2000, seed = 3) lp_held <- data.frame(lower = lp_ts$conf.low, upper = lp_ts$conf.high)[held, ] round(c(log_mean_95 = covers(lp_held, d2$eta[held]),         counts_90   = covers(pi90(yrep_ts[, held]), d2$y[held])), 2) #> log_mean_95   counts_90  #>           1           1 iv <- pi90(yrep_ts) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) for (s in c(1, 2)) {   r <- d2$site == s   plot(d2$year[r], d2$y[r], pch = ifelse(held[r], 1, 19),        ylim = c(0, max(d2$y[r], iv$upper[r])), xlab = "year",        ylab = "count", main = paste("site", s))   lines(d2$year[r], exp(lp_ts$estimate[r]), lwd = 2, col = "steelblue")   h <- r & held   arrows(d2$year[h], iv$lower[h], d2$year[h], iv$upper[h], angle = 90,          code = 3, length = 0.03, col = "darkorange")   abline(v = c(11.5, 13.5, 25.5), col = "grey70", lty = 3) } par(op)

code: matern1 <- function(h, range, sigma) {   kh <- sqrt(8) / range * h   ifelse(h == 0, sigma^2, sigma^2 * kh * besselK(kh, 1)) } set.seed(11) pts  <- data.frame(lon = runif(310), lat = runif(310)) g1   <- seq(1 / 60, 59 / 60, length.out = 30) grid <- expand.grid(lon = g1, lat = g1) K <- matern1(as.matrix(dist(rbind(pts, grid))), range = 0.3, sigma = 0.8) w <- as.numeric(t(chol(K + diag(1e-8, nrow(K)))) %*% rnorm(nrow(K))) pts$elev  <- rnorm(310) pts$eta <- 0.5 + 0.4 * pts$elev + w[1:310] pts$y   <- rpois(310, exp(pts$eta)) obs <- pts[1:250, ] out <- pts[251:310, ] mesh <- spatial_spde(~ lon + lat, data = obs, max_edge = c(0.1, 0.4),                      cutoff = 0.03) ctl <- list(n_threads = 2, progress = FALSE) fit_sp <- tulpa(y ~ elev, data = obs, family = "poisson", spatial = mesh,                 control = ctl) spatial_range(fit_sp) #>            mean        sd      q2.5     q97.5 #> range 0.2828414       Inf 0.1397424 0.5611945 #> sigma 0.6189089 0.1184173 0.4352965 0.8876350 p_sp  <- predict(fit_sp, newdata = out, se.fit = TRUE) p_fix <- predict(fit_sp, newdata = out, se.fit = TRUE, include_field = FALSE) data.frame(   prediction = c("with field", "fixed effects only"),   rmse       = round(c(sqrt(mean((p_sp$fit - out$eta)^2)),                        sqrt(mean((p_fix$fit - out$eta)^2))), 2),   coverage   = round(c(covers(p_sp, out$eta), covers(p_fix, out$eta)), 2)) #>           prediction rmse coverage #> 1         with field 0.39     0.92 #> 2 fixed effects only 0.61     0.47 fit_nngp <- tulpa(y ~ elev, data = obs, family = "poisson",                   spatial = spatial_gp(~ lon + lat), control = ctl) fit_hsgp <- tulpa(y ~ elev, data = obs, family = "poisson",                   spatial = spatial_gp(~ lon + lat, approx = "hsgp"),                   control = ctl) p_gp <- list(spde = p_sp,              nngp = predict(fit_nngp, newdata = out, se.fit = TRUE),              hsgp = predict(fit_hsgp, newdata = out, se.fit = TRUE)) tab_gp <- t(sapply(p_gp, function(p) c(   rmse = sqrt(mean((p$fit - out$eta)^2)), coverage = covers(p, out$eta),   width = mean(p$upper - p$lower)))) round(tab_gp, 2) #>      rmse coverage width #> spde 0.39     0.92  1.37 #> nngp 0.40     0.95  1.73 #> hsgp 0.40     0.95  1.57

code: GRID <- exp(seq(log(0.2), log(1.5), length.out = 7)) PHI  <- 0.7 BETA <- c(-0.2, 0.7)  simulate_one <- function(seed) {   set.seed(seed)   sigma  <- GRID[sample.int(length(GRID), 1L)]   region <- rep(seq_len(6L), each = 4L)   X      <- cbind(1, rnorm(24L))   u      <- rnorm(6L, 0, sigma)   list(y      = as.numeric(X %*% BETA) + u[region] + rnorm(24L, 0, PHI),        X      = X,        region = region,        theta  = c(beta1 = BETA[1], beta2 = BETA[2], sigma = sigma)) }  fit_one <- function(d, diagnose = FALSE) {   tulpa_nested_laplace(     y = d$y, n_trials = rep(1L, length(d$y)), X = d$X,     prior = list(list(type = "iid", obs_idx = d$region,                       n_units = max(d$region), sigma_grid = GRID)),     family = "gaussian", phi = PHI^2,     control = list(n_threads = 1L, keep_grid_hessians = TRUE,                    auto_recenter = FALSE, progress = FALSE,                    diagnose_k = diagnose, diagnose_skew = diagnose)) }

code: set.seed(3) n <- 200 d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n), w = rnorm(n)) d$y <- 0.5 + 1.0 * d$x + 0.3 * d$z + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) phi <- 0.64 s   <- 2 exact_posterior <- function(X, y, beta = 1) {   P <- beta * crossprod(X) / phi + diag(ncol(X)) / s^2   V <- chol2inv(chol(P))   m <- V %*% (beta * crossprod(X, y) / phi)   list(mean = drop(m), V = V) } X_xz <- model.matrix(~ x + z, d) ep <- exact_posterior(X_xz, d$y) fit_xz <- tulpa(y ~ x + z, data = d, family = "gaussian", mode = "smc",                 phi = phi, beta_prior = list(mean = 0, sd = s),                 control = list(wbic = TRUE, n_particles = 1000L,                                seed = 1L)) sm <- coef(summary(fit_xz)) data.frame(row.names  = rownames(sm),            smc_mean   = round(sm[, "estimate"], 4),            exact_mean = round(ep$mean, 4),            smc_sd     = round(sm[, "std.error"], 4),            exact_sd   = round(sqrt(diag(ep$V)), 4)) #>             smc_mean exact_mean smc_sd exact_sd #> (Intercept)   0.4109     0.4137 0.0559   0.0566 #> x             0.9628     0.9624 0.0572   0.0578 #> z             0.3167     0.3183 0.0565   0.0550

code: wbic(fit_xz) #> WBIC  238.61  (beta = 1 / log(200) = 0.1887, 1000 draws) exact_wbic <- function(X, y) {   tp <- exact_posterior(X, y, beta = 1 / log(length(y)))   r  <- y - X %*% tp$mean   length(y) / 2 * log(2 * pi * phi) +     (sum(r^2) + sum(diag(X %*% tp$V %*% t(X)))) / (2 * phi) } w3 <- c(smc_wbic   = wbic(fit_xz)$wbic,         exact_wbic = exact_wbic(X_xz, d$y),         neg_log_ev = neg_log_evidence(X_xz, d$y)) w3 #>   smc_wbic exact_wbic neg_log_ev  #>   238.6128   238.7974   241.7345 gap <- sapply(c(30, 100, 300, 1000), function(m) {   set.seed(2)   dm <- data.frame(x = rnorm(m))   dm$y <- 0.5 + dm$x + rnorm(m, sd = 0.8)   f <- tulpa(y ~ x, data = dm, mode = "smc", phi = phi,              beta_prior = list(mean = 0, sd = s),              control = list(wbic = TRUE, seed = 1L))   c(n = m, wbic = wbic(f)$wbic,     neg_log_ev = neg_log_evidence(model.matrix(~ x, dm), dm$y)) }) round(t(gap), 2) #>         n    wbic neg_log_ev #> [1,]   30   42.78      45.05 #> [2,]  100  121.86     124.22 #> [3,]  300  359.51     361.66 #> [4,] 1000 1195.71    1197.72

text: Put S=25S = 25 regions 5 5 lattice, adjacent regions sharing edge , observe T=10T = 10 time points. spatial truth u_true gradient rising south-west north-east corner, temporal truth v_true one sine wave ten time points. interaction hotspot south-west corner grows linearly time, centred regions time points satisfies sets constraints carries nothing main effects take. log scale three components standard deviations 0.6, 0.5 0.1. region-time cell gets one count intercept 1.5 (mean count 4.5) slope 0.4 covariate drawn per cell. data frame ordered region-fastest, row cell entry cell stacked interaction. show_map() draws one value per region lattice, south-west corner bottom left, value printed cell. true interaction three time points shows hotspot: negative time 1, positive time 10, opposite sign far corner centring puts .
code: nr <- 5; nc <- 5; S <- nr * nc; Tn <- 10 xy <- expand.grid(col = 1:nc, row = 1:nr) W  <- 1 * (as.matrix(dist(xy, method = "manhattan")) == 1) u_true <- 0.6 * as.numeric(scale(xy$col + 0.5 * xy$row)) v_true <- 0.5 * as.numeric(scale(sin(2 * pi * (1:Tn) / Tn))) g <- exp(-((xy$col - 1.5)^2 + (xy$row - 1.5)^2) / 2) bump <- 1.2 * outer(g, (1:Tn - 1) / (Tn - 1)) delta_true <- bump - outer(rowMeans(bump), rep(1, Tn)) -   outer(rep(1, S), colMeans(bump)) + mean(bump) round(c(range = range(delta_true), sd = sd(c(delta_true))), 3) #> range1 range2     sd  #> -0.358  0.358  0.107 set.seed(11) d <- expand.grid(region = 1:S, time = 1:Tn) d$cell <- seq_len(nrow(d)) d$x <- rnorm(nrow(d)) eta <- 1.5 + 0.4 * d$x + u_true[d$region] + v_true[d$time] +   delta_true[cbind(d$region, d$time)] d$y <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(eta)) head(d, 3) #>   region time cell           x y #> 1      1    1    1 -0.59103110 1 #> 2      2    1    2  0.02659437 2 #> 3      3    1    3 -1.51655310 2 show_map <- function(z, main, zlim, pal = hcl.colors(30, "Blue-Red 3")) {   image(1:nc, 1:nr, matrix(z, nc, nr), zlim = zlim, main = main, col = pal,         xlab = "", ylab = "", axes = FALSE)   text(xy$col, xy$row, sprintf("%.2f", z), cex = 0.6) } op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)) for (tt in c(1, 5, 10)) show_map(delta_true[, tt], paste("time", tt), c(-0.4, 0.4)) par(op)

code: eta_posterior <- function(fit) {   k <- which(fit$weights > 0)   w <- fit$weights[k] / sum(fit$weights[k])   E <- fit$fitted_eta[k, , drop = FALSE]   V <- fit$fitted_eta_var[k, , drop = FALSE]   m <- colSums(w * E)   data.frame(mean = m, sd = sqrt(colSums(w * (V + E^2)) - m^2)) } ep_add <- eta_posterior(fit_add) r_add  <- (d$y - exp(ep_add$mean)) / sqrt(exp(ep_add$mean)) sw <- g > 0.3 r_mat <- matrix(r_add, S, Tn) plot(1:Tn, colMeans(r_mat[sw, ]), type = "b", pch = 19,      ylim = range(colMeans(r_mat[sw, ]), -1, 1),      xlab = "time", ylab = "mean Pearson residual") lines(1:Tn, colMeans(r_mat[!sw, ]), type = "b", pch = 1, lty = 2) abline(h = 0, col = "grey60") legend("topleft", c("south-west regions", "other regions"),        pch = c(19, 1), lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n") slope <- apply(r_mat, 1, function(r) coef(lm(r ~ seq_len(Tn)))[2]) moran_i(slope, as.matrix(xy), weights = "knn", k = 4) #>  #>  Moran's I (k=4 nearest neighbours) #>  #> data:  slope #> Moran's I = 0.21049, Expected I = -0.041667, p-value = 0.03726 #> alternative hypothesis: two.sided test_dispersion(fit_add, nsim = 100) #>  #>  Simulation-based dispersion test #>  #> data:  fit_add #> dispersion ratio = 1.0909, p-value = 0.44 #> alternative hypothesis: two.sided

code: held <- d$time > 8 d_na <- d d_na$y[held] <- NA fp_add <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = d_na, family = "poisson",                 spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),                 temporal = temporal_rw1("time"), mode = "auto", control = ctl) fp_II  <- fit_int("II", data = d_na) forecast_st <- function(fit, n = 2000) {   yrep <- posterior_predict(fit, ndraws = n, seed = 3)[, held]   data.frame(region = d$region[held], time = d$time[held], y = d$y[held],              lo = apply(yrep, 2, quantile, 0.05),              hi = apply(yrep, 2, quantile, 0.95)) } fc <- list(additive = forecast_st(fp_add), type_II = forecast_st(fp_II)) t(sapply(fc, function(f) c(covered = sum(f$y >= f$lo & f$y <= f$hi),                            of = nrow(f), mean_width = mean(f$hi - f$lo)))) #>          covered of mean_width #> additive      42 50      6.801 #> type_II       42 50      6.841 ep_past <- eta_posterior(fp_II) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1)) for (s in c(1, 25)) {   ys <- d$y[d$region == s]   f_a <- fc$additive[fc$additive$region == s, ]   f_2 <- fc$type_II[fc$type_II$region == s, ]   plot(1:Tn, ys, pch = 19, ylim = c(0, max(ys, f_2$hi, f_a$hi)),        xlab = "time", ylab = "count", main = paste("region", s))   lines(1:8, exp(ep_past$mean[d$region == s & !held]), lwd = 2)   arrows(9:10 - 0.1, f_a$lo, 9:10 - 0.1, f_a$hi, angle = 90, code = 3,          length = 0.03, lty = 2)   arrows(9:10 + 0.1, f_2$lo, 9:10 + 0.1, f_2$hi, angle = 90, code = 3,          length = 0.03, col = "steelblue")   abline(v = 8.5, col = "grey60") } par(op)

code: R_s <- Matrix(diag(rowSums(W)) - W, sparse = TRUE) R_t <- Matrix(crossprod(diff(diag(Tn))), sparse = TRUE) B_IV <- rbind(kronecker(matrix(1, 1, Tn), diag(S)),               kronecker(diag(Tn), matrix(1, 1, S))) st_block <- function(K, B, name, mean = 3, sd = 1.5, lower = 0, upper = 7) {   C <- 1e3 * Matrix(crossprod(B), sparse = TRUE)   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) as(as(exp(theta[1]) * K + C, "generalMatrix"),                            "CsparseMatrix"),     prior = function(theta) dnorm(theta[1], mean, sd, log = TRUE),     init = c(log_tau = mean), bounds = list(lower = lower, upper = upper),     obs_idx = d$cell, name = name) } fit_blk <- function(blk) {   tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region) + latent(blk), data = d, family = "poisson",         spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),         temporal = temporal_rw1("time"), mode = "auto", control = ctl) } fit_wide  <- fit_blk(st_block(kronecker(R_t, R_s), B_IV, "IV wide")) fit_tight <- fit_blk(st_block(kronecker(R_t, R_s), B_IV, "IV tight",                               mean = 6, sd = 0.25)) hp <- function(f) summary(f)$hyperparameters[3, c("mean", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")] rbind(wide = hp(fit_wide), tight = hp(fit_tight)) #>           mean    ci_lo    ci_hi #> wide  3.667326 2.620556 5.098760 #> tight 5.929250 5.439626 6.429674 blk_delta <- function(fit) {   g <- tulpa_outer_grid(fit)   cols <- g$n_fixed + S + Tn + seq_len(S * Tn)   matrix(colSums(g$weights * g$modes)[cols], S, Tn) } M_wide <- blk_delta(fit_wide); M_tight <- blk_delta(fit_tight) round(c(cor_wide = cor(c(M_wide), c(delta_true)),         cor_tight = cor(c(M_tight), c(delta_true)),         sd_wide = sd(c(M_wide)), sd_tight = sd(c(M_tight)),         sd_true = sd(c(delta_true))), 3) #>  cor_wide cor_tight   sd_wide  sd_tight   sd_true  #>     0.778     0.840     0.100     0.025     0.107 fit_flat <- fit_st_nested(d$y, cbind(1, d$x), d$region, W, d$time, Tn,                           temporal_type = "rw1", family = "poisson",                           hyperprior = "flat", control = list(n_threads = 2)) rbind(proper = summary(fit_st)$hyperparameters[1:2, c("median", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")],       flat = summary(fit_flat)$hyperparameters[1:2, c("median", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")]) #>             median    ci_lo     ci_hi #> proper.1  4.785948 2.449798  8.666083 #> proper.2  9.800275 3.134236 24.986984 #> flat.1    4.858475 2.476467  8.809522 #> flat.2   10.518826 3.371556 26.591536

code: time_fit <- function(nside, Tk, type_IV = FALSE) {   xy_k <- expand.grid(col = 1:nside, row = 1:nside); Sk <- nrow(xy_k)   W_k <- 1 * (as.matrix(dist(xy_k, method = "manhattan")) == 1)   dk <- expand.grid(region = 1:Sk, time = 1:Tk); dk$x <- rnorm(nrow(dk))   dk$y <- rpois(nrow(dk), exp(1 + 0.4 * dk$x + 0.3 * sin(dk$region) +                                 0.3 * cos(dk$time)))   st <- if (type_IV) spatiotemporal(type = "IV")   el <- system.time(fk <- tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = dk,     family = "poisson", spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W_k),     temporal = temporal_rw1("time"), spatiotemporal = st, mode = "auto",     control = ctl))   c(regions = Sk, times = Tk, grid_cells = nrow(tulpa_outer_grid(fk)$nodes),     seconds = round(el[["elapsed"]], 1)) } set.seed(5) cost <- rbind(time_fit(5, 10), time_fit(6, 10), time_fit(5, 20),               time_fit(5, 10, TRUE), time_fit(6, 10, TRUE),               time_fit(5, 20, TRUE)) cost #>      regions times grid_cells seconds #> [1,]      25    10        126     0.3 #> [2,]      36    10        156     0.3 #> [3,]      25    20        144     0.4 #> [4,]      25    10        944    19.1 #> [5,]      36    10        693    27.0 #> [6,]      25    20        662    36.7

text: Put 64 regions 8 8 lattice, adjacent regions share edge . W adjacency matrix xy holds lattice coordinates region. sim_areal() draws smooth surface s lattice exponential covariance range 3 cells, standardised mean 0 SD 1. covariate region rho * s plus independent noise, standardised , rho = 0.8 correlates surface. region holds six observations binomial count 20 trials, conditional slope beta = 1 field gamma * s gamma = 0.8. function returns data truths: beta_c slope used simulate, beta_m adds slope regression field covariate observations. seed marginal slope two thirds larger conditional one, covariate shares much variation field.
code: k  <- 8 xy <- cbind(rep(1:k, k), rep(1:k, each = k)) W  <- 1 * (as.matrix(dist(xy)) == 1) dim(W) #> [1] 64 64 sim_areal <- function(seed, beta = 1, gamma = 0.8, rho = 0.8, m = 6) {   set.seed(seed)   K  <- exp(-as.matrix(dist(xy)) / 3) + diag(1e-8, nrow(xy))   s  <- as.numeric(scale(t(chol(K)) %*% rnorm(nrow(xy))))   xr <- as.numeric(scale(rho * s + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(nrow(xy))))   region <- rep(seq_len(nrow(xy)), each = m)   w  <- gamma * s[region]   x  <- xr[region]   y  <- rbinom(length(x), 20, plogis(-0.2 + beta * x + w))   list(d = data.frame(y = y, x = x, region = region),        beta_c = beta, beta_m = beta + coef(lm(w ~ x))[["x"]]) } sim <- sim_areal(1) c(conditional = sim$beta_c, marginal = sim$beta_m) #> conditional    marginal  #>    1.000000    1.672309

code: three_fits <- function(sim, spec, f_sp, n_trials) {   fits <- list(     unrestricted = tulpa(f_sp, data = sim$d, family = "binomial",                          n_trials = n_trials, spatial = spec,                          mode = "nested_laplace", control = ctl),     restricted = tulpa(f_sp, data = sim$d, family = "binomial",                        n_trials = n_trials,                        spatial = spatial_rsr(spec, restrict_to = ~ x),                        mode = "nested_laplace", control = ctl),     nonspatial = tulpa(y ~ x, data = sim$d, family = "binomial",                        n_trials = n_trials, mode = "laplace"))   tab <- t(sapply(fits, function(f) unlist(coef(summary(f))["x", c(1, 3, 4)])))   data.frame(fit = rownames(tab), est = tab[, 1], lo = tab[, 2],              hi = tab[, 3], beta_c = sim$beta_c, beta_m = sim$beta_m) } areal <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:4, function(seed) {   cbind(seed = seed, three_fits(sim_areal(seed), car, y ~ x + spatial(region),                                 rep(20L, 384))) })) plot_slopes <- function(res, main) {   fits <- c("unrestricted", "restricted", "nonspatial")   pch  <- c(1, 17, 15)   col  <- c("grey40", "darkorange", "steelblue")   ypos <- res$seed + (match(res$fit, fits) - 2) * 0.22   plot(res$est, ypos, xlim = range(0.8, res$lo, res$hi), yaxt = "n",        pch = pch[match(res$fit, fits)], col = col[match(res$fit, fits)],        xlab = "slope of x", ylab = "seed", main = main)   axis(2, at = unique(res$seed))   segments(res$lo, ypos, res$hi, ypos, col = col[match(res$fit, fits)])   abline(v = res$beta_c[1], lty = 2)   bm <- unique(res[, c("seed", "beta_m")])   segments(bm$beta_m, bm$seed - 0.4, bm$beta_m, bm$seed + 0.4, lwd = 2)   legend("bottomleft", fits, pch = pch, col = col, bty = "n", cex = 0.8) } plot_slopes(areal, "ICAR field on an 8 x 8 lattice") err <- function(res) {   sapply(split(res, res$fit), function(r) {     c(to_conditional = mean(abs(r$est - r$beta_c)),       to_marginal    = mean(abs(r$est - r$beta_m)))   }) } round(err(areal), 3) #>                nonspatial restricted unrestricted #> to_conditional      0.602      0.652        0.520 #> to_marginal         0.076      0.030        0.127 covers <- function(res) {   sapply(split(res, res$fit), function(r) {     c(conditional = mean(r$lo <= r$beta_c & r$beta_c <= r$hi),       marginal    = mean(r$lo <= r$beta_m & r$beta_m <= r$hi))   }) } covers(areal) #>             nonspatial restricted unrestricted #> conditional        0.0          0         0.00 #> marginal           0.5          1         0.75

Build the RSR field on spatial_car() / spatial_car_proper() / spatial_bym2() / spatial_gp(), or drop spatial_rsr() and fit the field directly. sim_points <- function(seed, n = 150, beta = 1, gamma = 0.8, rho = 0.9) {   set.seed(seed)   lon <- runif(n); lat <- runif(n)   K <- exp(-as.matrix(dist(cbind(lon, lat))) / 0.25) + diag(1e-6, n)   s <- as.numeric(scale(t(chol(K)) %*% rnorm(n)))   x <- as.numeric(scale(rho * s + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(n)))   w <- gamma * s   y <- rbinom(n, 25, plogis(-0.2 + beta * x + w))   list(d = data.frame(lon = lon, lat = lat, x = x, y = y),        beta_c = beta, beta_m = beta + coef(lm(w ~ x))[["x"]]) } gp <- spatial_gp(~ lon + lat) points <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:4, function(seed) {   cbind(seed = seed, three_fits(sim_points(seed), gp, y ~ x, rep(25L, 150))) })) plot_slopes(points, "NNGP field, 150 locations") round(err(points), 3) #>                nonspatial restricted unrestricted #> to_conditional      0.732      0.745        0.651 #> to_marginal         0.048      0.056        0.067 covers(points) #>             nonspatial restricted unrestricted #> conditional          0          0            0 #> marginal             1          1            1

code: matern1 <- function(h, range, sigma) {   kh <- sqrt(8) / range * h   ifelse(h == 0, sigma^2, sigma^2 * kh * besselK(kh, 1)) } set.seed(11) n    <- 300 obs  <- data.frame(lon = runif(n), lat = runif(n)) g1   <- seq(0.0125, 0.9875, length.out = 40) grid <- expand.grid(lon = g1, lat = g1) K    <- matern1(as.matrix(dist(rbind(obs, grid))), range = 0.3, sigma = 0.8) w    <- as.numeric(t(chol(K + diag(1e-8, nrow(K)))) %*% rnorm(nrow(K))) w_obs <- w[1:n]; w_grid <- w[-(1:n)] obs$x <- rnorm(n) obs$y <- rpois(n, exp(0.5 + 0.4 * obs$x + w_obs)) summary(obs$y) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>   0.000   0.000   1.000   1.957   3.000  22.000

predict(f, newdata = nd,                                               include_field = FALSE)   sqrt(mean((w_hat - w_grid)^2)) } tab <- t(sapply(fits, function(f) {   unlist(coef(summary(f))["x", c("estimate", "std.error")]) })) tab <- cbind(tab, seconds = time[rownames(tab)],              grid_rmse = c(sapply(fits[-2], field_rmse), nonspatial = NA)[rownames(tab)]) round(tab, 3) #>            estimate std.error seconds grid_rmse #> spde          0.329     0.049   10.01     0.433 #> nonspatial    0.402     0.042    0.01        NA #> nngp          0.334     0.051    4.54     0.431 #> hsgp          0.339     0.045    3.02     0.443 compare_models(nonspatial = fits$nonspatial, spde = fits$spde,                nngp = fits$nngp, hsgp = fits$hsgp, criterion = "waic") #>        model      elpd  se_elpd    p_eff        ic        delta   se_diff #> 3       nngp -494.9421 14.46039 71.91668  989.8843    0.0000000        NA #> 2       spde -495.8170 15.60920 61.98838  991.6340   -0.8748791  1.996046 #> 4       hsgp -500.2318 17.27644 49.13809 1000.4637   -5.2897024  4.437305 #> 1 nonspatial -664.1170 49.82610  7.82318 1328.2340 -169.1748583 44.758013 #>         weight #> 3 7.032568e-01 #> 2 2.931965e-01 #> 4 3.546707e-03 #> 1 2.373594e-74

code: periodic_ar1 <- function(n) {   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) {       sigma <- exp(theta[1]); rho <- tanh(theta[2])       d <- rep((1 + rho^2) / sigma^2, n)       o <- rep(-rho / sigma^2, n)       M <- Matrix::bandSparse(n, k = c(-1, 0, 1),                               diagonals = list(o, d, o))       M[1, n] <- M[n, 1] <- -rho / sigma^2     # wrap       methods::as(methods::as(M, "generalMatrix"), "CsparseMatrix")     },     prior = function(theta) {       dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE) +     # weak on log_sigma       dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)       # weak on atanh_rho     },     init   = c(log_sigma = 0, atanh_rho = atanh(0.3)),     bounds = list(lower = c(log(0.3), atanh(0.0)),                   upper = c(log(3.0), atanh(0.9))),     name   = "periodic_ar1"   ) }

what: A combination tulpa() does not fit yet
title: Troubleshooting
text: combinations terms refused fitting. random slope next spatial field one. temporal field one trend per panel group (group_var) next spatial field another. message names combination fit. random intercept place slope, spatial model runs.
code: tulpa(y ~ x + (1 + x | site) + spatial(region), data = ds,       family = "binomial", spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W)) #> Error: #> ! Random-slope term(s) together with a spatial field are not supported through tulpa() yet. Use a random intercept (1 | g) alongside the spatial term, or drop the spatial field. tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds, family = "binomial",       spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),       temporal = temporal_rw1("time", group_var = "site")) #> Error: #> ! A grouped (panel) temporal field cannot be combined with a spatial or latent(...) field through tulpa() yet (the joint path has no per-group temporal layout). Fit the panel temporal field on its own. fit <- tulpa(y ~ x + (1 | site) + spatial(region), data = ds,              family = "binomial",              spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),              mode = "laplace", sigma_re = 0.5) coef(fit) #> (Intercept)           x  #>  -0.2589096   0.9905863

code: tulpa(y ~ x + spatial(region), data = ds, family = "binomial",       spatial = list(type = "icar", adjacency = W),       temporal = temporal_rw1("time"),       control = list(max_grid_cells = 50, n_threads = 2)) #> Error: #> ! code: # A 3 x 3 regular grid of cell centres grid <- expand.grid(x = 1:3, y = 1:3) grid$cell <- paste0("c", seq_len(nrow(grid)))  g <- adjacency(grid, x_coord = "x", y_coord = "y", id = "cell",                type = "queen") g #> <tulpa_adjacency> #>   nodes: 9  edges: 20  (queen contiguity) #>   neighbours per node: min 3, mean 4.44, max 8 #>   cell size: x = 1, y = 1 #>   pass $adjacency to spatial(graph = ) and node_index() to remap data g$adjacency #> 9 x 9 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix" #>    c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7 c8 c9 #> c1  .  1  .  1  1  .  .  .  . #> c2  1  .  1  1  1  1  .  .  . #> c3  .  1  .  .  1  1  .  .  . #> c4  1  1  .  .  1  .  1  1  . #> c5  1  1  1  1  .  1  1  1  1 #> c6  .  1  1  .  1  .  .  1  1 #> c7  .  .  .  1  1  .  .  1  . #> c8  .  .  .  1  1  1  1  .  1 #> c9  .  .  .  .  1  1  .  1  .  # Second-order (24-neighbour) queen contiguity: any order is settable g2 <- adjacency(grid, id = "cell", order = 2)  # Advanced: a custom stencil (symmetrized for the undirected field) g3 <- adjacency(grid, id = "cell", offsets = list(c(1, 0), c(0, 1))) #> adjacency(): custom stencil was not symmetric; symmetrized to an undirected graph for the ICAR/CAR field (12 reverse edge(s) added). A directed neighbourhood cannot be represented by an undirected field.  # Use it in a model: graph stays explicit and inspectable spatial(graph = g$adjacency, formula = ~ 1 || cell_idx) #> tulpa areal varying-coefficient field #> ===================================== #>  #> Structure: ICAR (Besag)  #> Graph nodes: 9  #> Graph node index: cell_idx  #> Fields: independent (|| -> separate precision per coefficient) #> Expands to 1 CAR field(s) (one per design-matrix column): #>   cell_idx.Intercept  # Remap observation data (original cell ids -> 1:n node indices) by key obs <- data.frame(cell = c("c5", "c1", "c5", "c9")) obs$cell_idx <- node_index(g, obs$cell) obs #>   cell cell_idx #> 1   c5        5 #> 2   c1        1 #> 3   c5        5 #> 4   c9        9

title: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for one-RE GLMMs — agq_fit
text: Marginal-likelihood approximation generalised linear mixed model one cluster-level intercept random effect. Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (AGQ) generalises Laplace replacing single-point Gaussian integral around cluster's posterior mode n_quad-point quadrature. AGQ n_quad = 1 recovers Laplace approximation; higher n_quad reduces approximation error, especially clusters observations non-Gaussian likelihoods. engine block, front door: tuning knobs (max_iter, tol, n_quad) sit signature rather control list. Scoped lme4::glmer(..., nAGQ = N) use case: one intercept- RE term, families binomial, poisson, gaussian. multi-RE random-slope models, use tulpa_laplace() (Laplace joint mode) HMC.

title: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for one-RE GLMMs — agq_fit
code: set.seed(1) n_g <- 20; n_per <- 5; n <- n_g * n_per group <- rep(seq_len(n_g), each = n_per) x <- rnorm(n) X <- cbind(1, x) u <- rnorm(n_g, 0, 0.8) eta <- 0.3 + 0.7 * x + u[group] y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(eta))  # Compare Laplace (n_quad = 1) and AGQ-7. fit_lap <- agq_fit(y, X, group, family = "binomial", n_quad = 1) fit_agq <- agq_fit(y, X, group, family = "binomial", n_quad = 7) c(fit_lap$log_marginal, fit_agq$log_marginal) #> [1] -58.97289 -58.96207

title: Backend registry – single source of truth for the inference backends — BACKEND_REGISTRY
text: One entry per backend. Adding backend single entry ; tier membership, family support, input contract, R-level reachability derive list – single source truth per-tier backends family support. Fields: emits    – kind posterior representation backend's draws hold, fixes whether MCMC chain diagnostics apply (independent tier: exact SMC sampler emits "iid" particles, Tier-3 VI fit also emits "iid", nested-Laplace Tier-2 fit emits "iid" ): "chain" : autocorrelated MCMC output – Rhat autocorrelation-ESS meaningful (diagnostics() computes ). "iid"   : exchangeable draws deterministic approximation, resampled particles – split-Rhat vacuous ESS = n construction, say nothing approximation bias. "point" : posterior sample (mode + covariance ). tier     – tier key ("exact", "structured", "optimized"). input    – input contract backend's fitter consumes: "design"    : design-matrix bundle (y, n_trials, X, RE structure). "logpost"   : log_posterior(theta) closure plus dimension/init. "modeldata" : tulpa ModelData / LikelihoodSpec (C-ABI NUTS path). "nested"    : design-matrix bundle plus one latent prior blocks (latent(tgmrf(...))), integrated block hyperparameters nested-Laplace driver. "spde"      : design bundle plus self-contained SPDE spec (mesh + FEM matrices); fit_spde()'s CCD / grid hyperparameter engine. fitter   – name R function implementing backend, NULL C++ kernel exists R entry point yet. Stored string (function object) registry independent source-load order; resolved lazily via resolve_backend_fitter(). NULL => selectable R; dispatch fails loudly. families – character vector supported family identifiers, NULL unrestricted backend. cabi     – registered C-ABI callable backing backend (symbol model package reaches via LinkingTo: tulpa, one R wrapper call), NULL. carries_weights – TRUE "design" backend threads observation weights likelihood (non-spatially); absent otherwise. Every "logpost" backend carries log-posterior builder, .backend_carries_weights() one predicate reading . hyperprior – TRUE backend's fitter takes outer hyperprior = c("proper", "flat") choice tulpa() forwards; absent otherwise. note     – optional human-readable note. Family identity (families) checked family$name, family$distribution, family$numerator$distribution (tulpaRatio-style ratio families nest per-process distribution).

what: Central composite design (CCD) grid for nested-Laplace integration — ccd_grid
title: Central composite design (CCD) grid for nested-Laplace integration — ccd_grid
text: Produces structured set standardised hyperparameter points \(z \\mathbb{R}^k\) use integration nodes nested Laplace approximation \(k \ge 3\). CCD scales much better full tensor expand.grid() used 1D 2D backends: CCD \(1 + 2k + 2^{k - q}\) points (1 centre, 2k axial, \(2^{k - q}\) factorial), versus \(m^k\) m-per-axis tensor product. Point layout (centre+axial+factorial scaling \(f_0\)): 1 centre point origin; 2k axial points \(\pm f_0\) along coordinate axis; \(2^{k - q}\) factorial points corners hypercube, scaled lie sphere radius \(f_0\). \(k \le 6\) factorial portion full \(2^k\) design. \(k \ge 7\) half-fraction (\(q = 1\)) using defining word \(x_1 \cdots x_k\) keeps point count reasonable preserving Resolution V. Used tulpa_nested_laplace() higher-dimensional hyperparameter blocks. standardised z-coordinates mapped physical hyperparameters \(\theta\) via ccd_to_theta(). ccd_to_theta() converts standardised CCD z-coordinates (\(\mathbb{R}^k\)) physical hyperparameters \(\theta\) via affine map \(\theta = \hat\theta + L \cdot z\) optional log-scale transform per component. L typically Cholesky factor negative Hessian inverse evaluated (working) mode \(\hat\theta\) – .e. scales z one posterior standard deviation per axis. ccd_weights() gives per-point design weights ccd_grid() used nested-Laplace integration nodes. implements corrected R-INLA central-composite-design weights: formula Rue, Martino Chopin (2009) typo, corrected R-INLA team give positive central weight. m hyperparameters, np design points standardized scaling f0, every non-centre point gets $$w = 1 / ((np - 1)(1 + e^{-m f0^2 / 2}(f0^2 - 1)))$$ centre point gets \(w_0 = 1 - (np - 1) w\). Used \(\Delta_k\): integration weight node \(k\) \(\Delta_k \exp(\log\,\mathrm{marginal}_k)\), renormalized. standardized (whitened) hyperparameter posterior reproduce Gaussian moments exactly.

what: Compare models by information criteria — compare_models
title: Compare models by information criteria — compare_models
text: Rank fitted models best-first information criterion. "waic" "loo" use native pointwise log-likelihood layer (tulpa_criteria() / tulpa_psis()) – WAIC PSIS-LOO respectively, computed fit's [n_draws x n_obs] pointwise log-likelihood (fit$draws$log_lik), loo package dependency. "loglik" returns (integrated) joint log-likelihood parameter count. fit carrying pointwise log-likelihood (deterministic / point approximation) yields NA criterion columns rather error, table always one row per model. "wbic" ranks wbic(), estimate fit's negative log evidence, needs every fit carry tempered draws (mode = "smc", control = list(wbic = TRUE)); fit without gets NA row. evidence ("wbic", "loglik" wherever logLik() reports log marginal likelihood) integrates likelihood prior, moves prior's width way posterior hardly : widening prior SD factor c parameter data pin lowers log evidence log(c) per parameter. Two model types fitted different default priors therefore compared priors, likelihoods. ordinal fit, instance, puts N(0, 10^2) ridge cutpoint parameters (first cutpoint log gaps, cut_prior_sd tulpa_ordinal()) multinomial fit's class intercepts carry fixed-effect N(0, 2.5^2), part evidence gap two gap priors. Set priors statements defend models ranking evidence, rank "waic" / "loo", read posterior predictive depend prior posterior.

title: Compare models by information criteria — compare_models
text: data frame. "wbic" (ranked best-first): model, wbic, delta (WBIC gap best model, >= 0), weight (exp(-delta) normalized: posterior model probability equal prior model weights, log evidence read WBIC). "loglik": model, n_params, logLik, quantity conditioned_on (log-scale quantity logLik() reports, hyperparameters holds fixed; fits disagree either refused rather ranked). "waic" / "loo" (ranked best-first): model, elpd, se_elpd, p_eff, ic (-2 * elpd), delta (elpd gap best model), se_diff (SE pointwise elpd difference), weight (Akaike-style weight criterion).

code: # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("fmesher", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1)   n <- 200L   coords <- cbind(runif(n), runif(n))   mesh <- fmesher::fm_mesh_2d(loc = coords, max.edge = c(0.15, 0.4), cutoff = 0.05)   fem  <- fmesher::fm_fem(mesh)   A    <- as(fmesher::fm_basis(mesh, loc = coords), "CsparseMatrix")   spec <- spatial_spde_custom(C = fem$c0, G = fem$g1, A = A, nu = 1,                               prior_range = c(0.3, 0.5), prior_sigma = c(0.6, 0.05))   w <- as.numeric(rnorm(spec$n_mesh, 0, 0.6)); w <- w - mean(w)   x <- rnorm(n)   y <- rpois(n, exp(2.0 + 0.5 * x + as.numeric(spec$A %*% w)))   fit <- fit_spde(y = y, X = cbind(1, x), spatial = spec, family = "poisson")   fit$nested$range_mean } #> [nested-laplace] preparing joint Hessian sparsity pattern #> [nested-laplace] 1/441 cells (0%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=2s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 441/441 cells (100%) | elapsed 1s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells #> [1] 0.07330069 # }

title: Independence Metropolis-Hastings with Laplace proposal — imh_laplace
code: # Toy: Bernoulli logistic with one covariate. set.seed(1) n <- 100 x <- rnorm(n) eta <- 0.3 + 1.2 * x y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(eta)) X <- cbind(1, x)  lap <- tulpa_laplace(y, n_trials = rep(1L, n), X = X,                      family = "binomial")  log_post <- function(beta) {   eta <- as.numeric(X %*% beta)   sum(y * eta - log1p(exp(eta))) +     sum(dnorm(beta, 0, 10, log = TRUE)) }  fit <- imh_laplace(log_post, mode = lap$mode[1:2],                    hessian = lap$H_beta, n_iter = 1000) fit$mean_accept #> [1] 0.828 colMeans(fit$draws) #> [1] 0.4205109 1.2201961

title: Inference mode system — inference_modes
text: tulpa uses explicit tier system inference encodes epistemic guarantees, just runtime characteristics. design makes difference inference methods first-class unavoidable, rather hiding implementation details.

title: Inference mode system — inference_modes
text: Tier 1 - Exact: Asymptotically correct posterior inference (Monte Carlo error). Credible intervals interpretable posterior uncertainty. reference standard. Tier 2 - Structured: Accurate inference conditional explicit structural assumptions. Typically requires latent Gaussian structure, conditional independence, smooth posteriors. fast right model class, can wrong outside class. Failure modes predictable explainable. Tier 3 - Optimized: general correctness guarantee beyond empirical usefulness. Point estimates usually good, uncertainty often underestimated. Tails correlations unreliable. Failure usually silent. optimization, sampling.

title: Inference mode system — inference_modes

title: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: Sample posterior using MALA: Langevin proposal driven gradient log posterior, corrected Metropolis- Hastings accept/reject step. iteration one log-posterior + one gradient evaluation. natural stepping stone random-walk MH HMC: cheaper per iteration HMC (leapfrog integration), better-mixing RWMH drift term moves toward higher density. Step size epsilon adapted via dual averaging warmup target acceptance rate 0.574 (Roberts & Rosenthal 1998 optimal high-dimensional Gaussians).

title: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (MALA) — mala

title: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm (MALA) — mala
text: log_posterior Function function(theta) -> numeric returning unnormalized log posterior. grad_log_posterior Function function(theta) -> numeric vector returning gradient theta. init Numeric vector: initial state (must give finite log_posterior). n_iter Total iterations including warmup (default 2000). warmup Warmup iterations (step-size adaptation + discarded; default n_iter / 2). epsilon Initial step size (default 0.1). Adapted warmup. target_accept Target acceptance warmup adaptation (default 0.574, Roberts & Rosenthal 1998 optimum). mass_diag Optional preconditioner: length-d vector per-dimension variances, used diagonal inverse-mass M^-1. proposal N(theta + (eps^2/2) * M^-1 * grad, eps^2 * M^-1), entry j scales proposal variance along dimension j noise standard deviation eps * sqrt(mass_diag[j]). Default rep(1, d). posteriors different scales across dimensions, set (estimate ) posterior variances, .e. squared posterior SDs. mass_matrix Optional dense preconditioner: d x d symmetric positive-definite inverse mass M^-1, typically (estimate ) posterior covariance. proposal N(theta + (eps^2/2) * M^-1 * grad, eps^2 * M^-1), also reaches correlations diagonal : random-effect model fixed intercept group effects strongly correlated posteriori, identity diagonal metric crosses ridge rate narrowest direction. Supply one mass_diag / mass_matrix. thin Keep every thin-th post-warmup sample (default 1). seed Optional integer RNG seed. Scoped call: caller's .Random.seed restored exit, two calls seed give identical draws regardless surrounding RNG stream. verbose Print acceptance + step-size summary end (default FALSE).

title: MCMC diagnostic plots — mcmc_plots
text: Plots sampled fit's convergence exploration diagnostics: plot_rhat(): Rhat values parameters, colour-coded highlight convergence issues. Rhat values > 1.01 indicate potential convergence problems. plot_ess(): effective sample size (ESS) parameters, expressed ratio ESS total samples. Low ESS indicates high autocorrelation. plot_acf(): autocorrelation function (ACF) plots selected parameters. High autocorrelation indicates slow mixing low effective sample size. plot_pairs(): pairs plot bivariate relationships parameters. Divergent transitions (present) highlighted help identify problematic posterior regions. plot_divergences(): parallel coordinates scatter plots highlight parameter space divergent transitions occur. plot_energy(): overlaid histograms marginal energy (centred within chain) energy transition, along E-BFMI statistic. Low E-BFMI indicates poor exploration posterior.

title: Show default priors for a tulpa family — priors_default
text: family-specific overdispersion lines name ratio families model package registers (negbin_negbin, negbin_gamma, poisson_gamma, gamma_gamma, beta_binomial); among tulpa's family_names(). Default priors tulpa_priors() follow principles: Fixed effects (beta): Normal(0, 2.5) - weakly informative, allows coefficients roughly [-5, 5] link scale. Random effect SD (sigma): PC prior P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 - favors simpler models smaller variance components. Overdispersion (phi): PC prior P(phi > 10) = 0.01 NB2 size phi (larger phi less overdispersion; phi -> Inf Poisson limit). default keeps phi finite, allowing overdispersion penalising extreme values. Temporal correlation (rho): Beta(2, 2) - symmetric prior centered 0.5, appropriate AR(1) correlation. Spatial mixing (rho_spatial): Beta(1, 1) = Uniform(0, 1) - prior preference structured vs. unstructured spatial variation.

title: Show default priors for a tulpa family — priors_default
code: # Defaults for all families (no family argument) priors_default() #> Default priors for tulpa models #> ================================ #>  #> These are tulpa_priors()'s defaults: what prior_predict() and #> tulpa_simulate() draw from. tulpa() fits do not read them; their own #> defaults are listed at the end. #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0, 2.5) #>   Interpretation: Coefficients roughly in [-5, 5] on link scale #>   Customization: prior_normal(mean, sd) #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(sigma > 1) = 0.01 #>   Interpretation: Favors smaller variance components #>   Customization: prior_pc(U, alpha) or prior_half_normal(sd) #>  #> Overdispersion (phi) [negbin/poisson_gamma only]: #>   PC prior: P(phi > 10) = 0.01 #>   Interpretation: NB2 size; keeps phi finite (allows overdispersion), #>                   phi -> Inf is the Poisson limit #>   Customization: prior_pc(U, alpha) or prior_gamma(shape, rate) #>  #> Family-specific notes (model-package ratio families): #>   negbin_negbin: Uses phi for both processes #>   binomial: No overdispersion parameter (unless beta_binomial) #>   poisson_gamma: Uses phi for gamma shape parameter #>  #> What a tulpa() fit uses instead (set via beta_prior / re_prior): #>   Fixed effects: Normal(0, 2.5) on every backend #>   Random-effect SD: PC prior P(sigma > 3) = 0.01 (+ LKJ(2) on #>     correlations) on nested Laplace / re_cov_nested / eb; #>     half-Cauchy(2.5) on the samplers and mode = "gibbs"  # Family-specific defaults take a tulpa_family object. Model packages # (e.g. tulpaRatio) register rich families; a minimal one is enough here. fam <- tulpa_family(   name = "poisson_gamma",   simulate_fn = function(eta, params, n_obs, ...) rpois(n_obs, exp(eta[[1]])) ) priors_default(fam) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   )  # Including spatial parameters priors_default(fam, spatial = TRUE) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> Spatial mixing (rho_spatial): #>   Beta(1.00, 1.00)  [mean = 0.50] #>   Used for: BYM2 mixing proportion (structured vs. unstructured) #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   )  # Use as a starting point for customization my_priors <- priors_default(fam) #> Default priors for poisson_gamma family #> =====================================  #>  #> Fixed effects (beta): #>   Normal(0.00, 2.50) #>   Used for: All regression coefficients in all processes #>  #> Random effect SD (sigma): #>   PC prior: P(x > 1.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(4.605) #>   Used for: Standard deviation of group-level effects #>  #> Overdispersion (phi): #>   PC prior: P(x > 10.00) = 0.010 #>     => Exponential(0.461) #>   Used for: Gamma shape parameter for effort/exposure #>  #> To customize, use tulpa_priors(): #>   priors <- tulpa_priors( #>     beta = prior_normal(0, 1), #>     sigma = prior_pc(U = 0.5, alpha = 0.01) #>   ) my_priors$beta <- prior_normal(0, 1)  # title: Simulation-based residual tests — simulation_tests
text: Tests fitted model data simulated , simulation-based residual checks DHARMa package: test_uniformity(): model correct, PIT residuals follow Uniform(0, 1). Applies Kolmogorov-Smirnov test null. Equivalent DHARMa::testUniformity(). test_dispersion(): compares variance observed data variance expected fitted model (via simulation). Ratio > 1 = overdispersion; < 1 = underdispersion. Equivalent DHARMa::testDispersion(). test_outliers(): counts many observations fall outside min--max range simulations. correct model, expected number approximately 2 * N / (nsim + 1). Equivalent DHARMa::testOutliers(). test_zero_inflation(): compares number zeros observed data distribution expected fitted model. Equivalent DHARMa::testZeroInflation().

code: # Create adjacency matrix for 10 regions (chain structure) adj <- matrix(0, 10, 10) for (i in 1:9) {   adj[i, i+1] <- adj[i+1, i] <- 1 }  # Create BYM2 spatial structure bym2 <- spatial_bym2(adj, level = "group", group_var = "region") print(bym2) #> tulpa spatial specification #> =========================== #>  #> Type: BYM2  #> Level: group  #> Spatial units: 10  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  #> Group variable: region  #> Scale factor: 0.8169   # \donttest{ # Disease mapping with BYM2 spatial smoothing set.seed(456) n_regions <- 10 epi_data <- data.frame(   region = factor(rep(1:n_regions, each = 4)),   age = rnorm(n_regions * 4, 50, 10) ) epi_data$cases <- rbinom(nrow(epi_data), size = 100, prob = 0.15)  fit <- tulpa(   cases ~ age + spatial(region),   spatial = spatial_bym2(adj, level = "group", group_var = "region"),   data = epi_data,   family = "binomial",   n_trials = rep(100L, nrow(epi_data)),   mode = "laplace" ) summary(fit) #> tulpa fit  (laplace, tier 2)  #> Call: tulpa(formula = cases ~ age + spatial(region), data = epi_data, family = "binomial", mode = "laplace", n_trials = rep(100L, nrow(epi_data)), spatial = spatial_bym2(adj, level = "group", group_var = "region")) #>   inference mode: structured  #>   selected because: User-specified backend: laplace  #>   family: binomial  #>   n_obs: 40  #>  #> Fixed effects: #>              estimate std.error     2.5 %   97.5 % #> (Intercept) -1.924190  0.330895 -2.572733 -1.27565 #> age          0.006046  0.004658 -0.003084  0.01518 # }

title: Multi-scale Gaussian process spatial structure — spatial_multiscale
text: multi-scale model decomposes spatial variation additively: $$\eta(s) = X\beta + w_{local}(s) + w_{regional}(s)$$ component follows independent Gaussian process: $$w_{local}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{local} C(\phi_{local}))$$ $$w_{regional}(s) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2_{regional} C(\phi_{regional}))$$ Fitting. mode = "auto", "structured" "nested_laplace" fit field nested Laplace, two field blocks multi-block driver (two NNGP blocks, neighbour structure, two HSGP blocks one basis). scale carries SD range axes outer grid, placed refined like field axis, scales' variances ranges integrated. exact samplers (mode = "exact" siblings) sample NNGP form priors. spatial_range() reports scale's sigma range (3 * phi), tagged [local] / [regional]; field_effects() reports summed field per distinct location, one scale component =. Identifiability. fields proper, neither needs level constraint; constant share intercept held priors. tells scales apart range priors: regional field's PC prior puts 5% mass range_regional[1], local field's range_local[1], neither range bounded . data separate scales, local range can therefore reach regional interval two scales share variance, widens intervals rather switching labels. simulated Poisson data 300 locations 10 x 10 square (local SD 0.63 range 0.5, regional SD 1 range 3, range_local = c(0.2, 1.5), range_regional = c(1.5, 10)), nested 95% intervals four hyperparameters covered truth 5 data sets, posterior means 0.66 / 1.1 (local SD / range) 1.03 / 7.3 (regional); component maps correlated simulated fields 0.49 (local), 0.79 (regional) 0.85 (sum). Computational cost. data sets nested fit took 97-125 s (100 locations: 29 s). Exact NUTS 100 locations took 453 s 4 chains 1000 iterations converged (R-hat 1.14 bulk ESS 13 local log-variance), chains disagreeing variance splits scales.

code: # Create RSR spatial structure on an areal field W <- matrix(0, 4, 4) for (i in 1:3) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 rsr <- spatial_rsr(   spatial_car(W, level = "obs"),   restrict_to = ~ depth + temp ) print(rsr) #> tulpa spatial specification #> =========================== #>  #> Type: ICAR (Intrinsic CAR)  #> Level: obs  #> Spatial units: 4  #> Shared: Yes (enters both processes)  #>   (rho fixed at 1, sum-to-zero constraint applied) #>  #> Restricted Spatial Regression (RSR): #>   Orthogonal to: ~depth + temp  #>   (Spatial effect constrained to be orthogonal to covariate space)  # \donttest{ # Areal binomial data on a chain of regions, covariate spatially confounded set.seed(404) n_regions <- 12 W <- matrix(0, n_regions, n_regions) for (i in 1:(n_regions - 1)) W[i, i + 1] <- W[i + 1, i] <- 1 df <- data.frame(region = factor(rep(1:n_regions, each = 5))) df$x <- as.integer(df$region) / 4 + rnorm(nrow(df), 0, 0.5) df$y <- rbinom(nrow(df), 20, plogis(-0.5 + 0.6 * df$x))  # RSR orthogonalises the spatial field to x, protecting its coefficient fit <- tulpa(   y ~ x + spatial(region),   data = df,   family = "binomial",   n_trials = rep(20L, nrow(df)),   spatial = spatial_rsr(spatial_car(W, level = "obs"), restrict_to = ~ x),   mode = "auto",   control = list(n_iter = 500L, warmup = 250L) ) #> Warning: tulpa(): the 'gibbs' chain has not converged -- log_tau_spatial: Rhat 1.00, bulk-ESS 35. Its estimates and intervals are not yet the posterior. Run longer (control$n_iter / control$warmup), or use mode = 'hmc'; see check_diagnostics(). summary(fit) #> tulpa fit  (gibbs, tier 1)  #> Call: tulpa(formula = y ~ x + spatial(region), data = df, family = "binomial", mode = "auto", n_trials = rep(20L, nrow(df)), spatial = spatial_rsr(spatial_car(W, level = "obs"), restrict_to = ~x), control = list(n_iter = 500L, warmup = 250L)) #>   inference mode: exact  #>   selected because: rsr spatial model (binomial Polya-Gamma Gibbs)  #>   family: binomial  #>   n_obs: 60  #>   posterior draws: 250  #>  #> Fixed effects: #>             estimate std.error   2.5 %   97.5 % #> (Intercept)  -0.3073   0.11586 -0.5143 -0.06732 #> x             0.5257   0.06116  0.4166  0.64575 #>  #> Fixed-effect prior: normal(0, 2.5) #>  #> Reliability (chain draws): #>   max Rhat 1.026, min bulk-ESS 34.72, min tail-ESS 87.51 #>   verdict: not converged #>  #> WARNING: chain not converged (max Rhat 1.00, min bulk-ESS 35 on log_tau_spatial); #>   these estimates are not yet the posterior.
