title: Gaussian process temporal structure — temporal_gp
text: GP temporal model adds time-correlated random effect: $$\eta(t) = X\beta + f(t)$$ \(f(t)\) follows Gaussian process: $$f(t) \sim GP(0, \sigma^2 C(|t - t'|; \phi))$$ correlation function \(C(d; \phi)\) depends time distance \(d\): Exponential: \(C(d) = \exp(-d/\phi)\) - continuous differentiable Matern: Smooth tunable roughness via \(\nu\) Gaussian: \(C(d) = \exp(-(d/\phi)^2)\) - infinitely differentiable Periodic: \(C(d) = \exp(-2\sin^2(\pi d/p)/\phi^2)\) - seasonal data Implementation: exponential kernel (equivalently Matern nu = 0.5) Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, joint density factorizes first-order Markov chain evaluates O(T) matrix. kernels finite-dimensional state-space form evaluated dense T x T Cholesky, T number distinct time points. field fit sampler path: two hyperparameters (log_sigma2_temporal_gp, logit_phi_temporal_gp) sampled jointly field fixed effects, pass sampler mode mode = "hmc". nested-Laplace kernel .

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
text: Gaussian latent block z ~ N(mu(theta), Q(theta)^{-1}): $$\log p(z\mid\theta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\det Q(\theta) - \tfrac{1}{2}(z - \mu(\theta))^\top Q(\theta)(z - \mu(\theta)) + \mathrm{const}$$ gradient -Q(z - mu) Hessian -Q wrt z closed form, user never writes gradient code. Laplace inner step needs Q(theta) mu(theta) numeric theta. Marginal NUTS VI use finite differences inner Laplace marginal; every additional target evaluation costs inner mode solve. Pseudo-marginal IMH corrects approximation unbiased importance integration. Marginal NUTS uses PSIS correction gate; tulpa_tgmrf() records fit's target.

title: User-defined GMRF latent block — tgmrf
code: # Periodic AR(1) block, wrap-around tridiagonal precision. periodic_ar1 <- function(n) {   tgmrf(     Q = function(theta) {       sigma <- exp(theta[1]); rho <- tanh(theta[2])       d <- rep((1 + rho^2) / sigma^2, n)       o <- rep(-rho / sigma^2, n)       M <- Matrix::bandSparse(         n, k = c(-1, 0, 1), diagonals = list(o, d, o)       )       M[1, n] <- M[n, 1] <- -rho / sigma^2       methods::as(M, "CsparseMatrix")     },     prior = function(theta) {       stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE) +         stats::dnorm(theta[2], 0, 1, log = TRUE)     },     init = c(log_sigma = 0, atanh_rho = 0),     name = "periodic_ar1"   ) }  blk <- periodic_ar1(20) print(blk) #> <tgmrf> "periodic_ar1" #>   n_latent : 20 #>   theta    : 2 dim (log_sigma, atanh_rho) #>   init     : 0, 0 #>   Q nnz    : 20 (5% of dense) #>   backend  : r

title: tulpa: Templated Unified Library for Posterior Approximation in Bayesian Hierarchical Models — tulpa-package
text: general-purpose engine fitting Bayesian hierarchical models spatial fields, temporal effects, spatially varying coefficients, multiple inference backends. Scalable spatial structure includes Hilbert space approximate Gaussian processes (HSGP; Riutort-Mayol et al. 2023 doi:10.1007/s11222-022-10167-2 ), nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes (NNGP; Datta et al. 2016 doi:10.1080/01621459.2015.1044091 ), intrinsic conditional autoregressive models (ICAR; Besag, York, Mollie 1991 doi:10.1007/BF00116466 ), reparameterized Besag-York-Mollie model (BYM2; Riebler et al. 2016 doi:10.1177/0962280216660421 ), stochastic partial differential equation fields (SPDE; Lindgren, Rue, Lindstrom 2011 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2011.00777.x ). Temporal structure covers random walks, autoregressive processes, Gaussian processes. Inference tiered correctness guarantee: exact Hamiltonian Monte Carlo -U-Turn sampler, Laplace nested Laplace approximations hyperparameter integration (Rue, Martino, Chopin 2009 doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2008.00700.x ), variational inference. Model-specific packages plug observation likelihoods engine templated C++ callback interface.

Random slopes supported Laplace (Tier 2) path: scalar sigma_re condition , RE covariance Sigma integrated rather fixed. covers correlated terms ((1 + x | g), full Sigma), uncorrelated terms ((1 + x || g), diagonal Sigma), several terms together ((1 + x | g) + (1 | h)) – term becomes covariance block, accompanying (1 | g) term integrated 1x1 block (nothing silently conditioned sigma_re = 1). mode = "laplace" routes nested-Laplace Sigma integrator (tulpa_re_cov_nested(), CCD design, PC + LKJ hyperprior default – see hyperprior); control$re_cov = "gibbs" switches exact Metropolis-within-Gibbs debias (tulpa_re_cov_gibbs()), control$re_cov = "aghq" keeps nested integrator replaces inner joint-Laplace marginal adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (control$n_quad, default 9 ; see n_quad tulpa_re_cov_nested()). also run sampler path (mode = "mala" / "pathfinder"). mode = "gibbs" (Polya-Gamma) fits single random-intercept model family = "binomial" "neg_binomial_2", samples RE sd rather conditioning sigma_re; tune via re_prior$prior_sigma_scale mean-zero beta_prior. Latent prior blocks (latent(tgmrf(...))) route nested-Laplace path (Tier 2), integrates block hyperparameters. mode = "auto" "structured" select automatically latent blocks present; mode = "nested_laplace" forces . Several random-intercept (1 | g) terms may accompany blocks; one-term restriction belongs Polya-Gamma spatial Gibbs sampler (mode = "gibbs"), updates one RE block alongside field. Joint multi-arm nested models expressed single-response formula – call tulpa_nested_laplace_joint() directly. ModelData sampler kernels ("hmc", "ess", "sghmc", "sgld", "mclmc", "smc", "vi") thread full latent vector – fixed effects, random effects (forms), areal spatial (icar / bym2), temporal (rw1 / rw2 / ar1) – one ModelData builder sample variance components jointly field. ess carries random effects declines structured spatial / temporal block (isotropic Gaussian-prior block represent graph precision); continuous-coordinate fields (gp / nngp / hsgp / spde), car_proper, exotic latent blocks stay dedicated nested-Laplace / SPDE / Polya-Gamma paths.

title: Fit a latent-variable model via EM + Laplace approximation — tulpa_em_laplace
code: # \donttest{ # Zero-inflated Poisson via EM: the E-step scores the posterior probability # that each zero is non-structural. Those are soft labels, so the occupancy # arm is the weighted Bernoulli above -- two rows per unit -- and the # abundance arm weights each count by the same w. set.seed(1) n <- 200 z <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.7) y <- rpois(n, 4) * z X <- cbind(1, rnorm(n))  e_step <- function(fits, ...) {   if (!length(fits)) return(list(weights = pmax(as.numeric(y > 0), 0.5)))   psi <- plogis(drop(X %*% fits$occ$mode))   lam <- exp(drop(X %*% fits$abund$mode))   w <- ifelse(y > 0, 1, psi * exp(-lam) / (psi * exp(-lam) + (1 - psi)))   list(weights = w) } m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) {   list(     occ   = list(y = rep(c(1, 0), each = n), X = rbind(X, X),                  weights = c(weights, 1 - weights), family = "binomial"),     abund = list(y = y, X = X, family = "poisson", weights = weights)   ) }  res <- tulpa_em_laplace(e_step, m_step_encode, verbose = FALSE) res$converged #> [1] TRUE plogis(res$fits$occ$mode[1])    # P(non-structural), truth 0.7 #> [1] 0.7034743 exp(res$fits$abund$mode[1])     # abundance mean, truth 4 #> [1] 3.871112 # }

title: Generic Monte-Carlo EM driver — tulpa_em_mc
code: # \donttest{ # Two-component Gaussian mixture with unit variances: the latent class z is # sampled in the E-step, and each class mean is an intercept-only Gaussian # block in the M-step. set.seed(1) z <- rbinom(100, 1, 0.4) y <- ifelse(z == 0, rnorm(100, -1), rnorm(100, 2))  e_step_sample <- function(fits, n_mc, ...) {   p1 <- if (length(fits) == 0L) {     ifelse(y > median(y), 0.8, 0.2)   } else {     l0 <- dnorm(y, fits$comp0$mode[1], log = TRUE) + log(0.6)     l1 <- dnorm(y, fits$comp1$mode[1], log = TRUE) + log(0.4)     1 / (1 + exp(l0 - l1))   }   lapply(seq_len(n_mc), function(s) rbinom(length(y), 1, p1)) } m_step_encode <- function(weights, ...) {   list(comp0 = list(y = y[weights == 0], X = matrix(1, sum(weights == 0), 1),                     family = "gaussian"),        comp1 = list(y = y[weights == 1], X = matrix(1, sum(weights == 1), 1),                     family = "gaussian")) }  fit <- tulpa_em_mc(e_step_sample, m_step_encode, n_mc = 5L, max_iter = 8L,                    verbose = FALSE) sapply(fit$pooled, function(p) p$mean) #>      comp0      comp1  #> -0.9868029  2.0396015  fit$history #>   iter n_mc      delta      mcse swamped #> 1    1    5        Inf 0.2545194      NA #> 2    2    5 3.72095902 0.2674963   FALSE #> 3    3    5 0.57057074 0.1697500   FALSE #> 4    4    5 0.23660514 0.2233103    TRUE #> 5    5    7 0.07377956 0.1868036    TRUE #> 6    6   10 0.28729681 0.1028114   FALSE #> 7    7   10 0.21766243 0.1472689    TRUE #> 8    8   14 0.22858400 0.1046445   FALSE # }

code: # Integrate a Gaussian linear model's residual SD: inner_fit(hypers) returns # the per-cell log marginal and the conditional fixed-effect posterior, and # the axis spec names the grid. tulpa_nested_laplace() is the packaged driver # built on this. set.seed(1) n <- 40L; X <- cbind(1, rnorm(n)); y <- as.numeric(X %*% c(0.5, -1) + rnorm(n)) XtX <- crossprod(X); Xty <- crossprod(X, y) inner_fit <- function(hypers) {   sigma <- as.numeric(hypers["sigma"])   V <- chol2inv(chol(XtX / sigma^2 + diag(1e-4, 2)))   mu <- as.numeric(V %*% (Xty / sigma^2))   list(log_marginal = -n * log(sigma) - 0.5 * sum((y - X %*% mu)^2) / sigma^2 +          0.5 * as.numeric(determinant(V)$modulus),        beta_mean = stats::setNames(mu, c("b0", "b1")), beta_cov = V) } specs <- list(hyper_axis_spec("sigma", grid = exp(seq(log(0.5), log(2),                                                       length.out = 9)),                               log_scale = TRUE, bounds = c(0, Inf))) res <- tulpa_hyper_grid(specs, inner_fit, n_draws = 500L, seed = 1L) res$theta_median #>     sigma  #> 0.9210447  res$beta #>         b0         b1  #>  0.5982129 -0.7603655

code: # Poisson counts with a shared latent factor and one free intercept per # species, the intercepts updated by a closed-form Newton step. set.seed(1) Ns <- 40L; S <- 5L lam <- matrix(rnorm(S, 0, 0.7), S, 1L) y <- matrix(rpois(Ns * S, exp(0.5 + tcrossprod(rnorm(Ns), lam))), Ns, S) oracle <- list(   working = function(eta) list(score = y - exp(eta), curv = exp(eta)),   ll_cell = function(eta, idx = NULL) {     if (!is.null(idx)) { eta <- eta[idx, , drop = FALSE]; yy <- y[idx, , drop = FALSE] }     else yy <- y     yy * eta - exp(eta)   },   data_ll = function(eta) sum(y * eta - exp(eta))) em_fit <- function(site_off, fac_off, em_prev) {   b <- if (is.null(em_prev)) rep(0, S) else em_prev   for (it in 1:20) b <- b + colSums(y - exp(outer(rep(1, Ns), b) + fac_off)) /     colSums(exp(outer(rep(1, Ns), b) + fac_off))   b } res <- tulpa_latent_ascent(   make_oracle = function(em) oracle, em_fit = em_fit,   offset_of = function(b) outer(rep(1, Ns), b), n_sites = Ns, n_species = S,   factors = list(zeta = matrix(scale(cos(seq_len(Ns)))[, 1], Ns, 1L),                  lambda = matrix(0.1, S, 1L)),   control = list(max_outer = 3L, factor_starts = 2L)) cor(res$factor$lambda, lam) #>            [,1] #> [1,] -0.9759935

text: Generic outer-grid nested Laplace driver. Temporal: "rw1", "rw2" (1D grid tau), "ar1" (2D (tau, rho)) SPDE continuous spatial: see cpp_nested_laplace_spde() (separate entry, rebuilds Q via SPDE Q-builder).

title: Nested Laplace approximation for latent Gaussian models — print.tulpa_nested_laplace
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) S <- 30L                                   # spatial units arranged in a chain nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setdiff(c(s - 1L, s + 1L), c(0L, S + 1L))) nn <- lengths(nb) field <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(S, 0, 0.4))))   # smooth spatial field idx <- rep(seq_len(S), each = 6L); n <- length(idx); x <- rnorm(n) y <- rbinom(n, 1L, plogis(-0.2 + 0.6 * x + field[idx])) prior <- list(type = "icar", n_spatial_units = S, spatial_idx = idx,               adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)), adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L,               n_neighbors = nn, tau_grid = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)) fit <- tulpa_nested_laplace(y, rep(1L, n), cbind(1, x), prior = prior,                             family = "binomial") #> [nested-laplace] 1/5 cells (20%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace] 5/5 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells fit$theta_mean        # marginalized ICAR precision #> [1] Inf # }

title: Joint multi-likelihood nested Laplace approximation — print.tulpa_nested_laplace_joint
text: Outer-grid nested Laplace driver joint models – multiple response arms sharing one latent prior block, parameterized per-arm field amplitude (sigma) unit-precision latent. Supported priors: "bym2"       – outer grid (sigma, rho [, alpha]). Latent: phi (n_s) | theta (n_s) unit-precision ICAR + iid components. "icar"       – outer grid (sigma [, alpha]). Latent: phi (n_s) unit-precision ICAR. "car_proper" – outer grid (sigma, rho_car [, alpha]). Latent: phi (n_s) Q = D - rho_car * W. backends (NNGP, HSGP, RW1/2, AR1) follow interface land Phase 3.

title: Joint multi-likelihood nested Laplace approximation — print.tulpa_nested_laplace_joint
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) S <- 25L                                   # shared spatial units (chain graph) nb <- lapply(seq_len(S), function(s) setdiff(c(s - 1L, s + 1L), c(0L, S + 1L))) nn <- lengths(nb) field <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(S, 0, 0.4)))) mk_arm <- function(m, fam) {   si <- sample(S, m, replace = TRUE); x <- rnorm(m)   lin <- 0.2 + 0.5 * x + 0.8 * field[si]   y <- if (fam == "binomial") rbinom(m, 1L, plogis(lin)) else lin + rnorm(m, 0, 0.5)   list(y = as.numeric(y), n_trials = rep(1L, m), X = cbind(1, x),        spatial_idx = si, family = fam, phi = if (fam == "gaussian") 0.5 else 1) } prior <- list(type = "icar", n_spatial_units = S,               adj_row_ptr = c(0L, cumsum(nn)), adj_col_idx = unlist(nb) - 1L,               n_neighbors = nn, sigma_grid = c(0.3, 0.7, 1.4)) fit <- tulpa_nested_laplace_joint(   responses = list(occ = mk_arm(200L, "binomial"), pos = mk_arm(200L, "gaussian")),   prior = prior) #> [nested-laplace-joint] 1/3 cells (33%) | elapsed 0s | ETA >=0s | 0.00s/cells #> [nested-laplace-joint] 3/3 cells (100%) | elapsed 0s | ETA done | 0.00s/cells #> [outer placement] round 1/30 | 11 evals | |step| 0.181 | logpost -329.5951 | elapsed 0s | 0s/eval #> [outer placement] round 2/30 | 14 evals | Newton step 0.00545 sd | logpost -329.5951 | elapsed 0s | 0s/eval #> [outer placement] mode-find done | 14 evals | logpost -329.5951 | elapsed 0s | 0s/eval fit$theta_mean        # shared field amplitude, integrated across both arms #>     sigma  #> 0.3064632  # }

what: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite refinement of a grouped random-effect covariance — tulpa_re_aghq
title: Adaptive Gauss-Hermite refinement of a grouped random-effect covariance — tulpa_re_aghq
text: Refines generalized linear mixed model's fixed effects random-effect covariance replacing per-group Laplace integral n_quad-point adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (AGHQ). n_quad = 1 joint Laplace (glmer nAGQ = 1); higher n_quad reduces small-cluster attenuation variance components binary / count data. Unlike agq_fit() (intercept-RE, built-binomial/poisson/gaussian likelihoods), engine callback-driven: caller supplies per-group conditional likelihood, custom marginal (e.g. latent-state-integrated occupancy / detection likelihood, latent-abundance-integrated N-mixture marginal) refines quadrature. engine block, front door: model packages call programmatically, tuning knobs (max_iter, n_quad, keep) sit signature rather control list. engine structure-agnostic. integrates per-group marginal $$M_g = \int \exp\{\ell_g(b_g)\}\, N(b_g; 0, \Sigma)\, db_g,$$ \(b_g\) group's random-effect vector (dimension \(\sum_m c_m\) RE terms) \(\ell_g(b_g)\) group's conditional log-likelihood linear predictors perturbed \(b_g\). \(b_g\) enters likelihood – one linear predictor, several coupled arms different observation granularities (e.g. per-site abundance arm per-visit detection arm sharing species grouping) – lives entirely callback. engine needs, per group, value / gradient / Hessian \(\ell_g\) \(b_g\) (mode) \(\ell_g\) quadrature nodes (sum). fixed parameters theta log-Cholesky coordinates \(\Sigma\) optimized jointly \(\sum_g \log M_g\); standard errors come quadrature-marginal Hessian. Two callback forms select structure (supply exactly one): make_site – common single-arm, per-row-separable case (\(\ell_g(b_g) = \sum_{\g} \log f_i(\eta_i + Z_i b_g)\) one linear predictor \(\eta\)). engine builds oracle per-row marginal RE design Z . make_group – general / multi-arm case. caller supplies per-group b-space oracle directly, non-separable units (e.g. visits N-mixture site coupled shared latent count) random effects several arms handled engine change. Scope: one shared grouping factor across RE terms (per-group integral factorizes). total RE dimension per group small (quadrature grid n_quad^dim).

code: # \donttest{ # A per-row-separable binomial GLMM marginal supplied through `make_site`. l1pe <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, x + log1p(exp(-x)), log1p(exp(x))) make_binom_site <- function(X, y, nt) function(theta) {   eta_fixed <- as.numeric(X %*% theta)   list(eta_re = eta_fixed,        deriv = function(rows, eta) {          p <- plogis(eta)          list(logL = y[rows] * eta - nt[rows] * l1pe(eta),               d1 = y[rows] - nt[rows] * p, d2 = -nt[rows] * p * (1 - p))        },        lmat = function(rows, ETA) y[rows] * ETA - nt[rows] * l1pe(ETA)) } set.seed(1) ng <- 30L; npg <- 8L; n <- ng * npg g <- rep(seq_len(ng), each = npg); x <- rnorm(n) X <- cbind(1, x); nt <- rep(3L, n); u <- rnorm(ng, 0, 0.9) y <- rbinom(n, nt, plogis(0.3 + 0.7 * x + u[g])) fit <- tulpa_re_aghq(theta0 = c(0, 0),                      re_terms = list(list(idx = g, n_groups = ng, n_coefs = 1L)),                      Sigma0 = list(matrix(0.25, 1, 1)),                      make_site = make_binom_site(X, y, nt), n_obs = n, n_quad = 5L) sqrt(fit$Sigma_list[[1]][1, 1])     # adaptive-GHQ RE standard deviation #> [1] 0.796036 # }

code: # \donttest{ # An iid random intercept written as a tgmrf block over 15 groups; the # inference method is an argument, not a parallel verb. See the # custom-process article at https://gillescolling.com/tulpa/articles/tgmrf.html. set.seed(3) J <- 15L; g <- rep(seq_len(J), each = 6L); n <- length(g); x <- rnorm(n) y <- rpois(n, exp(0.3 + 0.5 * x + rnorm(J, 0, 0.6)[g])) blk <- tgmrf(   Q = function(theta) Matrix::Diagonal(J, exp(-2 * theta[1])),   prior = function(theta) stats::dnorm(theta[1], 0, 1, log = TRUE),   init = c(log_sigma = 0), obs_idx = g) fit <- tulpa_tgmrf(y, rep(1L, n), cbind(1, x), block = blk,                    family = "poisson", mode = "imh",                    control = list(n_iter = 300L, warmup = 150L)) mean(exp(fit$draws[, "log_sigma"]))   # posterior mean group SD #> [1] 0.6507754 # }

title: Widely applicable Bayesian information criterion (WBIC) — wbic
text: Watanabe's (2013) WBIC: expected negative log-likelihood posterior tempered inverse temperature beta = 1 / log(n), $$\mathrm{WBIC} = -E_\beta\left[\sum_{=1}^n \log p(y_i \mid \theta)\right],   \qquad p_\beta(\theta) \propto p(\theta) \prod_{=1}^n p(y_i \mid \theta)^\beta.$$ estimates Bayes free energy -log p(y), negative log evidence, shares asymptotic expansion O_p(1) terms singular models well regular ones – mixtures, reduced-rank latent-factor structure, variance component zero – BIC's (d / 2) log n penalty describe evidence. Lower better.

Non-finite fitting inputs. tulpa() now rejects NA/NaN/Inf response model matrix offending row, instead letting NaN propagate silently kernels (model built na.pass). svc(approx = "nngp") now rejects duplicated coordinates (distance-0 neighbour gave singular per-node covariance) rather failing silently downstream. title: tulpa 0.0.5
text: feat(nested-laplace): fits now record wall-clock runtime returned object fit$timing (gcol33/tulpa#48). named numeric seconds carrying total plus phase breakdown – setup (validation / encoding / grid construction), grid (inner Laplace solves scale grid size core count, including adaptive-refinement consistency passes), postproc (weight / moment / marginal assembly), diagnostics (outer Pareto-k-hat). Covers tulpa_nested_laplace() (single- multi-block) tulpa_nested_laplace_joint() (single- multi-block dispatch); consumer fits riding joint object inherit . new print method nested-Laplace classes surfaces one-line summary ("fit 5h 25m (grid 2h 09m)") alongside hyperparameters, grid size, outer Pareto-k-hat. perf(nested-laplace): sparse joint outer grid now runs parallel control$n_threads_outer (gcol33/tulpa#46, lever 2). previously forced serial outer loop, large field inner per-observation OpenMP parallelised cores idled. sparse driver now allocates per-outer-thread pool (Hessian builder, Newton scratch, arm specs, scatter index cache, DENSE_BASIS scratch) dispatches grid cells across n_threads_outer, matching dense driver. phi-grid dispersion axis parallel-safe: rewrites shared arms dispersion per cell, cell snapshots thread’s specs short critical lock-free Newton solve. memory guard clamps thread count replicated builders large (wide fields fall back fewer outer threads). Parallel-vs-serial parity (without phi axis) covered tests/testthat/test-nested-laplace-joint-sparse-parallel.R. perf(nested-laplace): grad-inner-Newton steps inner_refresh (gcol33/tulpa#46, lever 1b). factor-reuse step Hessian discarded, cell-coupling scatter now passes grad_only request CellCouplingSpec (new ABI-appended CellDerivs::grad_only): spec may skip negative-Hessian work (e.g. beta arm’s digamma/trigamma) emit exact gradient, kernel skips cross-arm Hessian scatter. Specs implement write full Hessian (correct, saving). gradient stays exact every step, converged mode unchanged – validated grad--honoring cell-coupling reuse test tests/testthat/test-nested-laplace-joint-inner-refresh.R. perf(nested-laplace): control$inner_refresh (default 1L) adds Shamanskii / chord-method Cholesky factor reuse sparse joint inner Newton (gcol33/tulpa#46). non-quadratic positive arm (e.g. beta cover arm) latent Hessian changes every inner iteration, default re-factorizes sparse Cholesky step – dominant per-grid-cell cost. inner_refresh = m > 1 re-factorizes every m-th inner step reuses cached factor (refreshing early reused solve fails). gradient exact every step step line-search safeguarded, converged mode unchanged final mode-pass Hessian (log_det, SEs) always fresh – path mode uses stale curvature. Applies sparse LM path; dense small-n_x path re-factorizes cheaply ignores . Bit-equivalence every-step default covered tests/testthat/test-nested-laplace-joint-inner-refresh.R. feat(nested-laplace): tulpa_posterior_draws(fit, idx, n) – generic posterior sampler grid-integrated joint nested-Laplace backend (inla.posterior.sample() analogue, gcol33/tulpa#44). Draws outer-grid mixture sum_k w_k N(m_k, V_k): draw picks grid cell integration weights, samples inner latent vector cell’s constrained Gaussian via stored sparse precision Q_csc_*_per_grid (requires control$store_Q = TRUE). ICAR / BYM2 field sum--zero constraint imposed conditioning kriging (Rue & Held 2005), per-cell marginal matches constrained inner-Laplace covariance exactly; single-block multi-block (multi-field trend) layouts handled. Sampling mixture – rather single moment-matched Gaussian – faithful primitive marginalizing nonlinear derived quantities (change occupancy, expected-cover products). Draws tagged iid. Tests tests/testthat/test-posterior-draws-joint.R. fix(nested-laplace): joint outer-grid cheap-pass prune (control$prune = TRUE) longer mis-ranks grid cells drops true posterior mode (gcol33/tulpa#43). screen previously ran single Newton step one global pilot mode every cell; inner latent mode moves substantially across outer grid (large spatial fields, wide sigma/rho/alpha ranges) one-step approximation mis-estimated far cells O(1e5) log-units inverted ranking, prune skip full solve actual mode. screen now rank-faithful chained sweep lattice: cell runs short Newton run warm-started previous screened cell’s quasi-mode, every cheap mode stays near cell’s true mode cheap ranking agrees full-solve ranking. fix(nested-laplace): added safety gate joint cheap-pass prune. cheap-screen argmax disagrees full-solve argmax, kept posterior collapses onto cell whose cheap-vs-full log-marginal gap large, fitter warns falls back full grid ($prune_fallback_triggered, $prune_fallback_reason) rather silently returning pruned answer. silently-wrong pruned posterior now impossible. feat(spde): fit_spde() reports outer Pareto-k-hat accuracy diagnostic ($pareto_k) integrated (range, sigma) hyperparameters – iid-fit counterpart Rhat. k-hat < 0.7 means Gaussian proposal integrator orients CCD/grid fits hyperparameter posterior; >= 0.7 flags skewed / heavy-tailed posterior grid misfits. Controlled diagnose_k (default TRUE) / k_samples (default 200), RNG-restored fit’s draws unchanged. feat(nested-laplace): joint backend (tulpa_nested_laplace_joint, single- multi-block) reports outer Pareto-k-hat heterogeneous hyperparameter space (gcol33/tulpa#42). block-type-aware per-axis transform unconstrains axis – positive scales log, BYM2 mixing weight logit, copy coefficient identity – summed log-Jacobians enter importance target. CAR_proper rho_car axis (support adjacency eigenvalue interval, guessable) declines quadrature ESS rather apply wrong transform. feat(nested-laplace): control$hessian selects inner-Newton curvature joint mixture Hessian – "lm" (default, diagonal-ridge escalation CHOLMOD factorizes), "psd" (eigen-clamp dense observed Hessian), "fisher" (complete-data expected information, PSD construction). feat(joint-laplace): cross-arm coupling via CellCouplingSpec registry (gcol33/tulpa#32). Consumer packages register per-cell coupling spec (e.g. tulpaObs’s cover-hurdle) two arms share latent field; cross-arm block assembled joint Hessian (tulpa_register_cell_coupling C callable, default "separable" always available).

title: tulpa 0.0.2
text: feat: tulpa_re_aghq() – callback-driven adaptive Gauss-Hermite refinement grouped random-effect covariance. Generalizes agq_fit() (intercept-RE, built-binomial/poisson/gaussian) random slopes correlated multi-coefficient blocks sharing one grouping factor, per-observation marginal likelihood supplied caller make_site callback. lets downstream package refine custom marginal (e.g. latent-state-integrated occupancy / detection likelihood) quadrature. Reuses existing log-Cholesky covariance parametrization (.re_cov_*), gauss_hermite_prob(), optional LKJ correlation penalty; fixed parameters chol(Sigma) optimized jointly exact-marginal log-likelihood, SEs marginal Hessian. Recovery tests tests/testthat/test-re-aghq.R.

R wrapper keeps pilot Laplace solve (starting values + proposal shapes) weighted-quantile summary. feat(re-cov): tulpa_re_cov_nested() gains n_quad – adaptive Gauss-Hermite refinement inner marginal. n_quad = 1 (default) keeps joint-field Laplace inner solve unchanged; n_quad > 1 routes inner solve shared compiled AGHQ engine (cpp_glmm_oracle_make + cpp_aghq_objective), per-group integral inside Sigma integration debiased quadrature (tulpa_re_aghq() correction applied grid), reducing small-cluster variance attenuation binary / low-count data. fixed effects integrated (profiled + fixed-effect Laplace term), reported fixed-effect posterior marginal (ML-II) one rather joint-mode (PQL) estimate. per-group integral factorizes one shared grouping factor, AGHQ requires ; crossed RE terms keep joint-field Laplace (n_quad > 1 errors). Fixed-effect SEs now joint marginal Hessian (marginalizing community-covariance uncertainty, closer spAbundance posterior) rather Sigma-plug-Schur complement. numerical knobs tol / inner_max / inner_tol dropped (engine owns mode-find); sigma_beta kept fixed-effect ridge. Poisson now. feat(nmix): tulpa_nmix_site_marginal() exposes per-site N-mixture marginal composable random-effect callback (eval / eval_beta / obs_info_block), tulpa_re_aghq() gained make_group path general / multi-arm case (per-group b-space oracle), custom marginal coupled arms different granularities – abundance / detection arms N-mixture site sharing species grouping – integrates quadrature. text: Closes tulpaRatio migration tracker (gcol33/tulpa#15). v12 gated legacy ratio body compute_log_post_impl<T> behind generic-layout check, Phase D removes body every consumer LegacyRatioData / LegacyRatioLayout. Dev tools tools/icar_collapsed_check.R tools/bym2_gradient_check.R also removed. Removed dispatcher branches (D-2). resolve_gradient_fn (src/hmc_gradient_dispatch.h) now resolves generic spec->gradient_fn / compute_gradient_generic_arena / compute_gradient_generic_numerical paths. Mode overrides (AUTODIFF_TAPE, AUTODIFF_ARENA, AUTODIFF_FWD) H-mode specialized fallthroughs gone. Callers reaching dispatcher n_processes == 0 get Rcpp::stop pointer entry. hmc_gradient_dispatch_predicates.h deleted. Removed log-posterior orchestrators’ legacy body (D-2). compute_log_post, compute_log_prior, compute_log_lik_only (src/hmc_sampler.cpp) now forward compute_log_post_generic_spec_double; accumulate_log_prior_and_state / accumulate_obs_log_lik body 5 hmc_sampler_log_prior_*.h fragments gone, along hmc_log_posterior_split.h. compute_log_post_impl<T> (src/log_post_impl.h) reduces forward T = double defensive T(0) -op autodiff T (arena AD now routes compute_log_post_generic<Var>). Removed gradient kernels (D-3, ~30 files, ~17 KLOC). hand-coded H-mode kernels (composite + 4 phases, vectorized + 5 fragments, analytical, autodiff, feature, gp, hsgp, msgp, svc, tvc, st, temporal_gp, ms_temporal, latent), collapsed-spatial machinery (hmc_icar_collapsed_* ×9, hmc_gp_collapsed_* ×5), legacy ratio likelihood (hmc_likelihood.h, hmc_observation_likelihood.h), legacy fallback gradients (compute_gradient_numerical / _autodiff / _arena / _forward / _numerical_impl) deleted. 6 log_post_impl_*_block.h fragments 2 Rcpp ModelData populators (model_data_rcpp.h, hmc_modeldata_builders.h) follow. verify_gradient_runtime now always uses compute_gradient_generic_numerical reference. Simplified samplers (D-4). compute_param_layout (src/hmc_param_layout.cpp) requires n_processes > 0; model packages place model-specific scalars (overdispersion etc.) LikelihoodSpec extra-parameter block layout.extra_offset. ESS’s build_gaussian_priors get_non_gaussian_params (src/ess_sampler.h) walk process_beta_start extra_offset . hmc_nuts_mass_init.cpp drops family-specific block-spec heuristics (NB+ICAR / Bin+ICAR forced DENSE, NB phi-pair 2×2 block) — re-introducing need LikelihoodSpec hint. ST_IV mass-matrix override disabled. precision-informed diagonal mass setup warmup end (src/hmc_nuts_chain_iter_nuts.h) reconstructed eta data.legacy.X_num_flat branched legacy ModelType. ST_IV chains now fall back adapted DIAG mass matrix override re-expressed spec->eta_weights_fn. One -op per chain warmup end; practical impact sampling efficiency small. Removed skipped tests. tests/testthat/test-log-post-split.R tests/testthat/test-hmc-modeldata-builders.R deleted (every test Phase-D skip). legacy-ratio gradient-check test test-spatial-car-proper.R removed; two R-side spatial_car_proper() construction tests stay. Cumulative numbers. Phase D-1..D-5 deletes ~57 files ~18 000 lines legacy ratio infrastructure across src/, inst/include/tulpa/, tests/, tools/. Net code reduction v13 maintenance window starts. Downstream rebuild notes: * tulpaRatio already routes generic LikelihoodSpec path via tulpa_bridge.cpp + per-family payloads lik_specs/ (B1+B2 migration); rebuild v13 headers, logic changes needed. * tulpaObs never used legacy ratio path; rebuild v13. * tulpaGlmm Day-22+ already targets generic path; rebuild v13.

what: tulpa 2026-05-11 — NNGP Laplace: full off-diagonal precision scatter
title: tulpa 2026-05-11 — NNGP Laplace: full off-diagonal precision scatter
text: laplace_mode_gp (spatial-/ ST-combo NNGP entries nested_laplace.cpp) now assemble full NNGP precision matrix Λ = (- )' D⁻¹ (- ) every Newton iteration, replacing diagonal--w approximation kept 1/v_i focal diagonal row. missed : gradient contribution neighbours (+a_{,k}·q_i/v_i), -diagonal Hessian entries (focal, neighbour_k) (neighbour_k, neighbour_kp), pairwise precision members every conditioning set. Newton mode w therefore shrunk toward zero pointwise field recovery smooth latent fields collapsed (cor ≈ 0). batch_nngp_scatter(..., alpha_out = nullptr) — backward-compatible extra optional output capturing per-row conditional regression weights (already computed internally; just exposed). apply_nngp_full_prior_dense — scatters full precision contribution dense (grad, H) pair via alpha + cv bundle. apply_nngp_full_prior_sparse — , SparseHessianBuilder. make_nngp_prior_sparsity_pattern — emits (row, col) pairs required back sparse path. Wired four scatter call sites: laplace_mode_gp dense Newton, laplace_mode_gp sparse Newton (pattern expansion), spatial-cpp_nested_laplace_nngp scatter lambda, make_nngp_spatial_ops::add_prior_at_k (ST-combo NNGP block). Log-prior calls (log_prior lambdas) unchanged — need cm cv, existing batch_nngp_scatter signature still supports without alpha_out. Effect (downstream measurement tulpaGlmm Day-31 smoke): cor(w_mean, f_true) jumps near zero ≈ 0.81 Pearson 120-location Poisson + smooth-GP simulation. β recovery unchanged. Additive: TULPA_ABI_VERSION bump (still v10). Public shim signatures unchanged; inner Laplace scatter upgraded. Downstream packages must rebuild commit pick new behaviour (source changes required).
